kikuyu: Nigūo ūgīe na kīambīrīria kiega gīa mīmera tīgīrīra wa handa mbura īhakuhī kura
english: To have a good start for the banana plants, planting should be timed to coincide with the on-set of rains.

kikuyu: Nī thuna irīkū ciagīrīire kūhandwo ūrīminī wa marigū?
english: Which suckers is suitable for planting on banana farming

kikuyu: Thura thuna iria njega itarī na marima ma mbūca
english: Choose healthy sword sucker of superior banana cultivars and make sure there are no signs of weevil tunnels on the chosen suckers.

kikuyu: Eheria mīrī yothe na gakothi ka igūru- gūīka ūū gūitagwo paring
english: Remove all roots and a thin outer layer of corm skin epidermis this is known as paring.

kikuyu: īkīra thuna hau harute ngothi maaī-ini mahiu rīa kahinda ga 30sec kana ūrinde kwa kahinda rīa 20sec
english: Place only the pared area of sucker in boiling water for 30 seconds or surface sterilized for 20 min in fungicide mixture.

kikuyu: Ruta thuna īria irī na dawa na ūrenge gacunjī ka īgūrū
english: Remove the sterilized sucker and cut the top part to produce the corm.

kikuyu: Tukania kilo 20 cia thumu ūhīte wega na tīīrī wa igūrū na ūtukanie wega irima-inī
english: Mix 20 kilograms of well rotten manure with top soil and put the mixture in the hole.

kikuyu: Iga mūmera waku irima-inī rīu
english: Place the paired treated corm in the hole with the mixture.

kikuyu: Hūthīra tīīrī wa thīinī kūihūria irima na ūthike mūmera na ūrikū wa sentimita 10 thīīnī wa tīīrī
english: Use the sub-soil to fill up the hole and bury the corm in the hole at 10 cm below the soil cover.

kikuyu: ūhadaga atīa marīgū ma mūciarithanio
english: How stablishment using tissue culture /macro propagated seedlings

kikuyu: Kūhanda marigū ma mūciarithanio
english: Establishment using tissue culture /macro propagated seedlings.

kikuyu: Ruta karatathi, na wūige mūmera waku tīīrī-ini na ūriku wa sentimita 30 irīma- ini hamwe na matukanio ūcio
english: Remove the plastic bag container and place the TC plant, 30 cm deep in the hole with the mixture.

kikuyu: Kūharīrīa mūgūnda wa marigū
english: Land preparation for bananas

kikuyu: ūtanahanda, kūrima ūrikītie kwendekithītio na ūcokerithie.
english: Before planting, deep soil cultivation by ploughing and harrowing is recommended.

kikuyu: Mūgūnda ndūbatīī gūkoruo na mītī, ithaka na ria
english: The fields should be free of trees, bushes and especially perennial weeds

kikuyu: marigū mabatiī gūtigithūkanio atīa?
english: What is the correct spacing for planting bananas?

kikuyu: īka maūndū maya mbura īhakuhī kuura;
english: Should be done at the onset of rains.

kikuyu: Nī handū harīkū hega ha kūhanda marigū?
english: What is the best site to plant bananas?

kikuyu: Thura handu harī na tīīrī mwega, riera riega ria kurīma marigū
english: Choose a location with suitable soil and climate conditions for banana cultivation.

kikuyu: marigū mendaga tīīrī uraikūrūkia wega maaī na mūirū mūnoru
english: Bananas prefer well-drained, loamy soil with good organic matter content.

kikuyu: marigū moyaga kahinda kaigana atīa gūkūra būrūri-inī wa Kenya?
english: How long does a banana take to mature in Kenya?

kikuyu: Irigū rīoyaga kīndū mīeri 12-18 gūkūra. Marigū no magethuo thutha wa thīkū 90-150
english: A plant takes roughly 12 to 18 months to mature. Fruits are ready for harvesting 90 – 150 days after.

kikuyu: marigū mabatiī gūtigithūkanio atīa?
english: What is the right spacing for banana?

kikuyu: īgerio iria ciīkītuo cionanagia īkīro njega cia marigū nīīkinyagīrwo mangītīgithokanio na ūraihu wa 1.8m x1.8m
english: Experiments carried out recently show that good quality banana and heavy bunch can be achieved by keeping the planting distance at 1.8 X 1.8 m.

kikuyu: Nigūo gūciara makīria tīgīthania na 1.2m x 1.5m
english: However, to get maximum yield plantation is done at 1.2 X 1.5 m.

kikuyu: High density nī kūhanda itina 4444-5555 hactare-inī īmwe
english: High Density Planting : High density planting is in practice to accommodate 4444 to 5555 plants per ha

kikuyu: Nī mweri ūrīkū mwega wa kūhanda marigū?
english: Which month is best for banana plantation?

kikuyu: marigū mahandituo mweri wa gatatū/kana nimakūraga wega na gūcīara wega makīria kūrī marīa mahandītuo thutha ūcio nginya Dithemba
english: Bananas planted in March/April made better growth and gave higher yields than those planted upto December.

kikuyu: Marigū marutaga kīro thutha wa thīkū 300 thutha wa kūhanda mwerī-inī wa gatatū/kana
english: Flowering occurred in less than 300 days after planting in March/April.

kikuyu: Kūruta kīro na gūciara nīigomagīruo rīrīa ikīro cia rūgarī irī thīī wa 750F
english: Growth and flower bud differentiation and fruit development were adversely affected, when the average temperature was below 750 F

kikuyu: Mītīgithūkanie na 2m -3m kuuma mūtī nginya irigū-inī. Tīgīrīra nī warīra mūcing'i gītina-inī nīguo mīrī mīerū ndīgathune nginya rīrīa ūkwnda.
english: Keep at least 2 to 3 meter gap between 2 plants. Also keep good mulch around the base , so that new root growth should not start new shoots until you want them.

kikuyu: Uthondekaga atīa mūgūnda mweru wa marigū?
english: Establishing a new banana garden?

kikuyu: Marigū mekaga wega nandū harī na tīīrī mūriku, uraikūrūkia wega maaī na mūnoru
english: A site with deep, well-drained and fertile soils, preferably rich in organic matter is good for banana production.

kikuyu: Nīgūteithagia mūmera kūgia hinya na guītirīa mīrīmū
english: It will encourage the development of strong plants that can tolerate infections.

kikuyu: Mūgūnda mwerū ūtarī na mīnyongoro kana mīrimū mīūru ya kūhoha, Fusarium wilt na bacterial wilt, nīwendetwo
english: A newly opened land without signs or history of nematodes or the devastating Fusarium wilt and bacterial wilt diseases is preferred.

kikuyu: Angīkorwo mūgūnda ūcio nīwarīmītwo marigū mīaka īrī mīhītūku, nīwega weherio marigū marīa matiga hamwe na thuna
english: If the site has been used for production of bananas in the last two years, it is highly recommended to remove all remaining banana plants and corms.

kikuyu: Matigari mau mahithaga tūtambi na mīrimū.
english: Normally such remnants harbour a lot of pests and diseases.

kikuyu: Matigari mau mabatīe meherio mūgūnda-inī na matwaro kūngī, matinangio na manīkuo nīguo mome
english: The remnants should be transferred into another field (not of bananas), chopped and spread to dry or composted.

kikuyu: Gūika ūū nīgūtigagīrīra tūtambi na mīrīmū yothe nīyeherio ūtanahada marigū merū.
english: This will ensure that any remaining pest or disease infections are completely removed before introducing new banana plants.

kikuyu: Ria rīothe rībatiī rīeherio ūtanahada nīūndū marigū nīmatoragio nī ria
english: All perennial weeds should also be removed and destroyed before planting because bananas are very susceptible to weed competition.

kikuyu: ūgītheria mūgūnda wa marigū tigīa mītī mīnini ya kūhinga rūhuho rūnene na rīua kūhe marigū kīruru marī manini.
english: Some of the existing trees at the selected site should be left during land clearing in order to protect the young banana plants from wind and strong direct sunshine

kikuyu: Ona angīkorūo gacunjī o gothe ka irigū no kahūthīke gūcīarithania nī thuna īhūthīkaga
english: Although any part of the banana plant can be used to generate tissue culture plants, it is the meristem/shoot tip that is commonly used

kikuyu: ūngīthondeka atīa marīgū ma mūciarithanio?
english: How to produce tissue culture banana plantlets

kikuyu: 1. Thura wega marigū maria ūgūciarithania matarī na mīrimū na tūtambi na marakūra narua. Onia arutuwo thuna ciothe, īmwe īrīa irī na mūrimū na īngī itarī. Matarīrie atī ndūngīkoruo na ūma kana nī mūrwaru kana ndūri mūrimu tondu thuna nyingī cionekaga īrī njega nginya rīrīa corms ikuoneka.
english: 1. Carefully select source materials (peepers or small sword suckers) that appear healthy (pest- and disease-free) and that are growing vigorously. [Trainer: Show two suckers to the participants: one that has visible evidence of pest or disease infestation and one that appears healthy. Explain that you cannot be sure if you are planting infected or clean material, as most suckers appear to be relatively healthy until their corms are exposed.]

kikuyu: 2. ūkīhūthīra icembe kana banga, tīgīthūkanīa thuna iria irendeka na mūramba
english: 2. Using either a hoe or a panga, separate the sucker (‘ex-plant’) from the mother plant.

kikuyu: 3. Thambia thuna ukīruta tīīri na ūtīnie mīrī nīgūo corms cioneke.
english: 3. Clean the sucker by removing soil and cutting off the roots to expose the corm.

kikuyu: Renga mūramba ūtigie sentimita 30.
english: Cut off parts of the pseudostem to a length of about 30 cm

kikuyu: 4. Banga īcunjī icio cia mūramba karatathi-inī ka munyore gatheru na ūcithamie nginya handū hangī hatheru.
english: 4. Pack the pseudostem parts in a clean nylon bag and transport them to a cleaner environment for further manipulation.

kikuyu: 5. Thambia thuna nīguo weherie ndoro na gīko kīngī.
english: 5. Wash the sucker under tap water to remove mud and other debris.

kikuyu: 6. Eheria mathangū mothe manathī, na ūrenge mūrita wa corm ūtigīe ūrī na ithimo cia 2cmx2cmx2cm ūnyitanīte na mūthia wa thuna.
english: 6. Trim away the outer leaf sheaths, leaf bases and corm tissue of the ex-plant until a 2 × 2 × 2 cm3 cube enclosing the shoot apex remains.

kikuyu: Menyerera ndūkarenge mūthia wa thuna
english: Be careful to avoid cutting through the apex.

kikuyu: 7. iga mūmera ūcio wa mbere wagūciarithania thīīni wa tūmīkebe
english: 7. The ex-plant is placed directly on a multiplication-inducing culture medium in containers.

kikuyu: Nigūo kūhanyūkia gūkūra nīyongagīrīruo cytokinin
english: A growth regulator (cytokinin) is added to the multiplication medium to speed up the process.

kikuyu: Mīkebe īyo īcoke īigwo thīinī wa incubators na ūrugarī wūigwo ūrī digirii 28 na ndūgakūre kana kūingīha na makīria ma digirii 2.
english: The containers are transferred to incubators or growth chambers and maintained at an optimal growth temperature of 28 ± 2°C. 8.

kikuyu: mīthia ya thuna cia marigū ma mūciarithanio nī majitagwo nī mūrimū wa kūira nī iria kuuma guraro-inī.
english: Banana tissue culture shoots often suffer from blackening caused by exudates from wounded tissues.

kikuyu: Iria rīrī rītarendeka rīthondekaga thingo iria igiragia thuna kūria irio na igatūma ciīkururie mūkūrīre-inī.
english: These undesirable exudates form a barrier round the tissue, preventing nutrient uptake and hindering growth.

kikuyu: Nigūo kūgīrīrīria, wiki cia mbere 4-6, thuna njerū nīicenjagio thutha wa wiki 1-2
english: To prevent this, during the first 4–6 weeks fresh shoots are transferred to new medium every 1–2 weeks.

kikuyu: Thuna kana ga kahīri gacio karīa gethondekete icokaga igathamīrio irio-inī itarareka thuna ingī ciīongerere no irateithia mīri īthondeke.(irio cia mīri)
english: 10.Individual shoots or shoot clumps that have formed are transferred to a nutrient medium which does not promote further shoot proliferation but stimulates root formation (rooting media).

kikuyu: Thutha wa kūruta mīrī, mīmera īyo noīrutwo laboratory nīguo yūmīrīrie
english: After rooting, plantlets are ready to leave the laboratory for weaning and hardening.

kikuyu: Ni wega kūiga natharī ya marigū ya thuna ciumanite na marigū ma mūciarithanio?
english: Is it okay to establish a banana orchard using suckers derived from tissue culture plants?

kikuyu: īī no wūige, nī kūri andu mendagia thuna icio ciumanite na marigū ma mūciarithanio
english: Yes, it is ok and there are several people who sell suckers from orchards that were started using tissue culture plants.

kikuyu: Ona kūrī oūguo rī, thuna ciumanite na marigū ma mūciarithanio no ta thuna iria ingi kwoguo nīigumagīrwo nī mīrimū na tūtambi o ta thuna iria īngī
english: However, suckers derived from tissue culture plants are just like any other suckers, and not pest- and disease-free.

kikuyu: Mūmera wa gūcīarithanio ūngīrorwo wega no ūciare na ūkūre narua gūkīra marigū ma kawaida ma thuna
english: If a tissue culture plant is managed very well, it will always fruit and mature faster than an ordinary sucker.

kikuyu: Kaingī ihūthagīra mīeri 9-12 itanahandwo
english: Usually, this takes 9–12 months after planting.

kikuyu: Mūgūnda wa marigū ūhūthīkaga kahinda karaihu kūringana na ūria ūroretwo na nī ūndū ūmwe onakorwo ūhandītwo na njīra ngūrani.
english: How long a banana plantation lasts depends on the level of management, and is the same whether started with tissue culture plantlets or other planting material.

kikuyu: Hihi thuna kuma mūti wa mūciarithanio no ciīrwo nī cia mūciarithanio?
english: Are suckers from tissue culture plant also called tissue culture plants?

kikuyu: Aca, marigū ma mūciarithanio mahandwo mūgūnda-inī, thuna īria īkūruta ti cia mūciarithanio nī thuna cia kawaida.
english: No. When a tissue culture plantlet is planted into the field, all the suckers it produces thereafter are not tissue culture plants, they are ordinary suckers.

kikuyu: īī marigū no makūrio na njīra īno ya mūciarithanio
english: Yes, all banana cultivars can be produced using tissue culture technology.

kikuyu: Niguo gutungata marigū ma mūciarithanio, he bata kurora thoko ūrīa īhana nīguo gūtigīrīra baita nīkuoneka
english: However, the management of a tissue culture laboratory will first assess the commercial potential of a demanded cultivar to ensure profits.

kikuyu: īrima rīa kūhanda marigū rīagīrīire kwenjwo rīigana atīa?
english: What is the standard size of a planting hole?

kikuyu: Nī ūndū wīkīkaga kwenja irima rīīgana 45cmx45cmx45cm
english: It is common practice to dig a hole measuring 45 cm × 45 cm × 45 cm.

kikuyu: Angīkorwo nī kūhanda marigū na kahūa, nī īhinda rīrīku riega rīa gūthura harīa marīma ma kahūa makwenjwo?
english: If intercropping banana and coffee, when is it best to demarcate the planting holes for coffee?

kikuyu: Nī wega kūgayūkania harīa marima ma kahūa na marigū makwenjwo hamwe
english: It is best to plan and demarcate the planting holes for both coffee and banana at the same time.

kikuyu: Na marigū no mahandwo mūthenya ūcio?
english: And can the bananas be planted on the same day?

kikuyu: Hatirī thīna kwenja irima rīa kūhanda na gūikīra thumu hamwe
english: It is fine to dig the planting hole and apply manure at the same time.

kikuyu: harī kūhanda mūthenya ūcio nī kūringanaga na mūthemba wa thumu
english: Whether you can also plant on the same day depends on the manure you are using.

kikuyu: Angīkoruo thumu ni mūniaru wega na ūgatukanio wega na tīri, ni wega kūhanda mūthenya ūcio
english: If the manure is very well dried and well mixed with the topsoil, then it is okay to plant on the same day

kikuyu: Njagīrīire gūitīīrīria maaī kamūmera ka marigū thikū cīgana thutha wa kūhanda
english: For how long should I water the banana plantlet after planting?

kikuyu: wega nigūitīīrīria nginya mūmera wambie kūruta mathangū merī
english: The best practice is to water until the plantlet starts developing new leaves.

kikuyu: Ona kūrī ūguo angīkorwo nī kūraura wega ndūbatīe gūitīīrīria maaī rīngī
english: However, you do not have to keep watering if it is raining sufficiently.

kikuyu: He bata ūrīku wa kwarīra marigū manini?
english: What is the significance of applying mulch around the newly planted bananas?

kikuyu: Gwika ūguo nīguo kūgirīrīria kūra kwa maaī
english: This is done to prevent water loss.

kikuyu: Tondū mīmera īno nī minini no yūme, īthūke kana īkue
english: As the plantlets are fragile immediately after planting, if they dry out they can become damaged or die.

kikuyu: Nī ihinda rīrīku rīega rīa kūhanda marigū- nī gatagatīini wa mbura kana itambītie?
english: When is the best time to plant the bananas – is it in the middle of the rainy season or at the onset?

kikuyu: Ihinda rīega makīrīa rīa kūhanda marigū nī rīrīa mbura īhakuhī kura
english: The best time to plant bananas is at the onset of the rainy season.

kikuyu: No wendekīthie kūhanda mbembe na marigū hamwe?
english: Would you recommend intercropping banana and maize?

kikuyu: Ndūtarītuo kūhanda mbembe na marigū hamwe tondū nīitharanaga ūtheri wa rīua.
english: It is not recommended to intercrop maize and banana since maize will compete with bananas for light.

kikuyu: Nīkīi gīatūmaga miaka 20 mīhetūku mīgūnda ya marīgū yaikaraga kahinda karaihu gūkīra rīu?
english: Why is it that in the past (20 years ago) banana fields lasted longer than they do today?

kikuyu: Nogūkoruo na itūmi nyingī ingītwīra nīkīī mūgūnda wa marigū wahūthīkaga kahinda karaihu mīaka ya thutha; mīrīmū yarī mīnini, (mūrimū ta Xanthomonas wilt ndīarīkuo) tīīrī warī mūnoru gukīra rīu na ūrūgarī dwarī mūingi.
english: There could be several reasons to explain why banana fields used to last longer in the past, such as less disease pressure (e.g. diseases like Xanthomonas wilt were not yet present), soil fertility was not as depleted as it is currently, and global warming was not as intense as it is now.

kikuyu: No angīkoruo nīūgutungata mūgūnda waku, marigū moyaga mīaka ikūmī
english: But if you take care of your banana field it should last for 10 years.

kikuyu: marigū no mahanduo gītuamba-inī kīri na maaī?
english: Can bananas be grown in swampy areas?

kikuyu: īī, no mahanduo gītuamba-inī angīkoruo tīīrī ndūgūikara na maaī kahinda karaihu
english: Yes, they can be grown in swampy areas, as long as the soil is not waterlogged for long periods.

kikuyu: Nī makinya marīkū ubatīe kūrūmīriīra thutha wa kūgetha?
english: What are the key steps in post-harvest handling of bananas?

kikuyu: ūkīgetha, getha ūbacīrīīre, banga na ūige marīgū maku handū harī rīera rīracera wega nīguo maikare kahinda karaihu.
english: Post-harvest handling includes careful harvesting, proper packaging, and storage in a cool, well-ventilated area to extend shelf life.

kikuyu: Batīe gūtigithūkania atīa mīmera ya marīgū mūgūnda-inī wakwa?
english: How far apart should I space banana plants in my plantation?

kikuyu: Ūngīendekithia atīa na nīkī: Kūruga kana gūcina?
english: What would you recommend and why: cooking or roasting types?

kikuyu: Ūū kūraringana na wendi wa mūrīmi
english: This totally depends on the farmer’s interest.

kikuyu: Ūtungata nī ūhanaine
english: The management practices are the same.

kikuyu: Nī tūtambi tūrīkū twa marigū tūīkaine makīrīa būrūri-inī wa Kenya?
english: What are the common pests that affect banana plants in Kenya?

kikuyu: Tūtambi twa marigū būrūri-inī wa Kenya nī hamwe na mboca cia marigū, mīnyongoro, ūme, thrips na mbumbuī.
english: Common banana pests in Kenya include banana weevils, nematodes, aphids, thrips, and spider mites.

kikuyu: Hihi mīthemba ya marigū nīītiragia mūrimū wa Black Sigatoka būrūri-inī wa Kenya?
english: Are there banana varieties resistant to Black Sigatoka in Kenya?

kikuyu: īī, mīthemba ya marigū ta FHIA-17 na FHIA-23, yonanītie gwitīria na Black Sigatoka.
english: Yes, some banana varieties, such as FHIA-17 and FHIA-23, have shown resistance to Black Sigatoka.

kikuyu: Hihi batīī gūitīīrīria marigū maaī maita maigana?
english: How often should I irrigate my banana plantation?

kikuyu: Maita marīa ūngīitīīrīrīa maaī kūringanaga na maundu matiganīte, o na kūri ūguo, marigū nīmabataraga maaī kaingī makīria hīndī ya riūa.
english: The frequency of irrigation depends on local conditions, but bananas generally require regular watering, especially during dry periods.

kikuyu: Hihi no wendekīthie harī mūrīmi gūītīīrīrīa maaī mūgūnda wake angīkoruo niarīīre mūcing'i?
english: Would you recommend a farmer to water his or her banana plantation even after mulching?

kikuyu: nī harī bata gūītīīrīria maaī ona ngīkorūo nī warīire mūcing'i. (no gūkorirwo mbura nyingī nīīraura)
english: Yes, it important to water the plantation even after mulching (unless there is plenty of rain).

kikuyu: Hihi nīmaūndū marīkū maria matūrigicīire magīrīire ūkūria-inī wa kabicī?
english: What optimal ecological requirements for cabbage?

kikuyu: mita 700 nginya mita 2,200 igūrū wa iria. Mbura ītanyihīire 500 mm na ūrugarī wa ithimo cia 16 degree Celsius
english: 700 – 2,200 metres above sea level altitude.At least 500 mm of rainfall.16 – 20 0C growing temperature.

kikuyu: Tīri ūraikūrūkia maaī wega kana tīri mūirū mūhinyu. Tīri mūnoru mūingī na ūrūrū wa gītagatī kuuma 6.0 pH nginya 6.5 pH.
english: Well drained sandy or silty loam soils.High organic matter content.pH range 6.0 – 6.5

kikuyu: Nī maūndū marīkū mabataranagia ūkūria-inī wa mboga būrūri-inī wa Kenya?
english: What are the growing requirements for cabbages in Kenya?

kikuyu: Mboga nī mūmera wa kūndū kūrī heho na ūbataraga ūrugarī wa ithimo cia kuuma 15°C nginya 20°C
english: Cabbage is a cool season crop which requires an optimum growth temperatures range of 15- 20° C.

kikuyu: Gūkūmba kwa mboga nīkūnyihaga ūrugarī ūngīthiī makīria ma 25°C
english: Head formation reduced at temperatures higher than 25 degrees Celsius.

kikuyu: Ībataranagia mbura ya kūigana kīmera gīothe.
english: It requires adequate well distributed rainfall.

kikuyu: Angīkorūo tīri ndūrī na wūigū wa kūigana, hebata gūitīīrīria maaī nīgūo kūehereria mūtangīko owothe ūngīrehwo nī wagi wa maaī.
english: If the levels are low, irrigation should be used to supplement and relive the moisture stress.

kikuyu: Hihi nī mūigana ūrīkū wa bataraitha wagīrīire kūhūthīrwo mūgūnda-inī wa mboga?
english: What is the recommended fertilizer rate for cabbage growing?

kikuyu: Īkīra ngundi igirī nginya ithatū cīa thumu o irima (ūū nīkuga ūkūhūthīra tani inyanya cia thumu kūhanda īka ya mboga) ūcoke wongerere ngūnīko īmwe ya cuba ya maaī(gramu ikūmi) ya bataraitha mūthemba wa DAP irima-inī rīu (ūū nīkuga kiro mīrongo īnana cia bataraitha nīikūhūthīka kūhanda mboga īka īmwe). DAP ndīagīrīirwo kūhūthīrwo mūgūnda-inī ūrīna tīri ūrūrītio nī acid, hūthīra bataraitha mīthemba ya DSP, TSP kana NPK.
english: Apply 2 – 3 handfuls of manure per planting hole (8 tons/īka) and 2 half-litre water bottle tops (10 g) of DAP per planting hole (80 kg/īka).DAP should not be applied on acid soils, use DSP, TSP or NPK .

kikuyu: O thumu ūrīa mūhīu wega noguo ūbatiī kūhūthīka nīguo kūgirīrīria kūrehe igunyū mūgūnda-ini.
english: Only thoroughly decomposed manure should be used to avoid possible introduction of cutworms in the field.

kikuyu: Bataraitha ya DAP yagīrīirwo gūtukanio wega na tīri nīguo ndīgacine mīūngūrwa
english: The DAP fertilizer should be mixed thoroughly with the soil to avoid possible scorching of the seedlings.

kikuyu: Bataraitha ya mathangū ni CAN na yagīrīirwo gūīkīrwo maita merī nī ūndū wa kūmenyerera gūte īrio cia bata harī mūmera na cīngīura kūhetūkīra maaī maingī kana uongerere ūrūrū tīri-ini.
english: The crop should be top dressed with CAN fertilizer in 2 splits to avoid nutrient loss through leaching as well as excessive soil salinity.

kikuyu: Rita rīa mbere yagīrīirwo nīguīkirwo gramu ikūmi harīo mūmera (100kg/īka) wiki 2-3 thutha wa kūhanda
english: The first split is applied at a rate of 10 g/plant (100 kg/īka) 2 – 3 weeks after transplanting.

kikuyu: Rita rīa kerī yagīrīirwo nīgūīkīrwo gramu 20 harīo mūmera (200kg/īka) rīrīa mboga īrakūnja.
english: The second split is applied at a rate of 20 gm/plant (200 kg/īka) at the onset of head formation.

kikuyu: ūkīhanda īkīra ngundi 2-3 cīa thumu o harī irima rīa kūhanda (tani 8 harī īka) na giramu ikūmi cia DAP o harī irima rīa kūhanda. (kilo 80 hari īka)
english: At planting, apply 2 – 3 handfuls of manure per planting hole (8 tons/īka) and (10 g) of DAP per planting hole (80 kg/īka).

kikuyu: Hihi ūnyihu wa Potasium wīyonanagia atīa harī Kabicī
english: What are the deficiencies of potassium in cabbage?

kikuyu: Potassium īngīnyīha harī mūmera nīigiragīrīria mboga gūkūmba wega. ūingi wayo nītumaga kabici yatūke
english: Potassium (K) deficiency can result in marginal necrosis and lower head quality, but its excess can cause the heads to open (NB: Fertilizer application rates is guided by soil and leaf analysis

kikuyu: Nī indo irīku cingītūmīka kwarīra kabici mūceni?
english: Which material should I use in cabbage mulching?

kikuyu: Nikī mboga ībataraga nīgetha ikūre wega?
english: What nutrients are important in cabbage production?

kikuyu: Mboga ībataraga bataraitha ya NPK nigetha īkūmbe wega.
english: Cabbage needs plenty of nutrients. NPK is needed for head formation.

kikuyu: No nitrogen nyingī no īgirie mboga īkumbe wega na kūbutha thīinī.
english: However, excess nitrogen (N) may cause loose head formation and internal decay.

kikuyu: Potassium īngīnyīha harī mūmera nīgiragīrīria mboga gūkūmba wega na īngīingīha no yatūke
english: Potassium (K) deficiency can result in marginal necrosis and lower head quality, but its excess can cause the heads to open.

kikuyu: Mūmera ūngīgīa sulphur nyingī ni unyihagia magnesium na boron.
english: The plants have high Sulfur requirement; sensitive to deficiencies of Calcium, Magnesium, and Boron.

kikuyu: Mboga ībataraga maaī maigana atīa nīguo īkūre?
english: What are the water requirements for cabbage production?

kikuyu: maaī marīa ībataraga ni mirimita 500.
english: The optimal amount of rainfall required for Cabbage during the growing period is 500 mm.

kikuyu: Gūitīīrīria maaī ūrīa kwagīrīire gūtūmaga kabici ikūre cigananīirie. Wagīrirwo nikūnyihia maaī oūrīa mboga īraneneha kugirīrīria gwatūka na nigetha kabici īnenehe.
english: Regular watering ensures uniform.Watering should be reduced as crop matures head formation, prevents head splitting and increases the size of the head.

kikuyu: ūgunyu mūingī nī utūmaga tīri ūnyihie Magnesium na phosphorus.
english: Excessive watering increases water logging hence deficiencies of Magnesium and Phosphorus.

kikuyu: Hūthīra njīra cia kūhe maaī ūgīthamagia nīguo ūhote kwīiga ūtheru. No ūhūthīre jeti, mīberethi ya kūhe maaī kana mītaro.
english: Use potable water for irrigation for food hygiene.Irrigation can be overhead, drip or furrow

kikuyu: Ingīgirīrīria ria atia ūrīmi-inī kabici?
english: How do I control weeds in cabbage production?

kikuyu: Kugirīrīria ria rīria rīrī inini nio njīra īrīa njega rītanathūkia na kūnina hinya wa mīmera.
english: Weed control is especially important early in the season when weed competition can substantially reduce vigor, uniformity, and overall yield.

kikuyu: Kūrīmīra nīgwabata makīria kīambīrīria-inī kīa kīmera rīrīa ria rīhotomagia mūkūrīre wa kabici na thutha-inī maciaro moothe.
english: Weed control is especially important early in the season when weed competition can substantially reduce vigor, uniformity, and overall yield.

kikuyu: Nīguo ūgīe na magetha mega ma kabici wagīrīirwo kūeheragia ria wega.
english: Optimal production of these Brassica leafy vegetables depends on successful weed control.

kikuyu: Ninjagīrīirwo kūeheria mahuti mothe ma mīmera īria īrahandītwo mbere ya kūhanda mboga?
english: Should I remove all crop residues of the previous crop from my filed before planting cabbage?

kikuyu: Mahuti mothe ma mīmera ya hau kabere yagīrīirwo nīgūcinwo kana gūthikuo irima-inī rīriku.
english: All crop residues should be removed and destroyed by burning or burying in deep pits.

kikuyu: Njīra īno īteithagīrīria kūnina tūtambi tūrīa tūrarī hau mbere, tūgunyu na mīrimu yothe īngītambio harī mīmera mīerū
english: This helps prevent last season’s pests including caterpillars, aphids and beetles re-infesting your new crop and also control fungal and bacterial diseases.

kikuyu: Tūngīgirīrīria ria atīa mūgunda-inī wa mboga?
english: How do I prevent weeds on my cabbage?

kikuyu: Kūharīria mīgūnda wega ta gūcimba na kūhūra hianyū
english: Thorough land preparation, example: by plowing and harrowing

kikuyu: īkīra bataraitha hakuhī na mūmera harīa hatarī na ria.
english: • Place the fertilizer where the crop has the access to it but the weeds do not.

kikuyu: Īno njīra īteithagia mūmera gūtharana na ria wega
english: This allows the crop to be more competitive with weeds.

kikuyu: Tigīrīra mītaro ya gūte maaī nī mītheru
english: • Maintain cleanliness on the drainage canals

kikuyu: Iga mūgūnda waku ūtarī na ihinga cia ria ūtangīkorwo ndūkwenda gūtheria na ūrenda gūthondeka imamo cia thū
english: • Keep the surroundings of your farm free of weeds, unless they are maintained and intended as habitat for natural enemies

kikuyu: Kwarīra: hūthīra mahuti ma mucere ta kwarīra nīguo kūgiria ria kūmera.
english: • Mulching: Use rice straw as mulch to partially control weed.

kikuyu: Banga mahuti ma mūcere gatagatī ka mīmera mūigana wa tani ithano harī hectare īmwe
english: Apply straw perpendicularly to the rows at a rate of 5 t/ha.

kikuyu: Arīra thikū nini thutha wa kūhanda
english: Apply mulch within a few days after transplanting.

kikuyu: ūgacenjania mīmera yaku ndūgacokie mūmera ūrī barī īmwe na ūcio uma ho
english: • Crop rotation. Do not continuously plant crucifers in the same field.

kikuyu: Ikara ūkiroraga mīmera yaku ihinda kwa ihinda
english: • Regularly monitor the status of your crops

kikuyu: Ni njira īrīkū cia macini kana cia moko cia kugirīrīria ria kabici- ini ?
english: What are the mechanical.physical ways of controlling weeds on my cabbages?

kikuyu: Ndukareke ria rīkūre nginya rīīkīre kīro
english: Do not let the weeds to flower.

kikuyu: Rīeherie rītanagīa kīro
english: Remove them from the field before they start to flower.

kikuyu: Ria rīrī na mbegū rītikaigirīrwo handū harī na thumu tondū mbegū ndīkuaga handū thumu ūrabutha.
english: Weeds bearing seeds should not be placed in compost since seeds may not be killed in the process of decomposition.

kikuyu: Ona kūrī ūguo rī, thumu no ūkorwo kīhumo kīa ria.
english: Otherwise, compost might be a source of reintroduction of weeds into your fields.

kikuyu: Gucimbūrania, kūrima na kwenyūranga ibūru.
english: • Hoeing, mowing, and cutting

kikuyu: Mboga īkūraga na mīeri 2-5 kuuma gūthamia tuta-inī kūringana na mūthemba kana kūrīa īkūrīirio.
english: Maturity Period: 2.5 – 4 months after transplanting depending on variety and location

kikuyu: Gūkūra : kīongo kiomīrīria
english: • Maturity: When the head becomes firm

kikuyu: Getha mboga itanakīria kahinda gagukura nīguo ndīgathūke.
english: • Cut heads at the base and leave the outer leaves to protect the head and keeping it fresh

kikuyu: Īka īkūraga kabici cigana atia?
english: What is the average yield of cabbages per īka?

kikuyu: Mūgūnda wa kūhanda mboga ūharagīrīrio atīa?
english: How to prepare land for planting?

kikuyu: Kabici ndirī mīri mīriku, kwoguo, hatiri bata wa kūrīma ūrikītie mūno.
english: Cabbage is a shallow rooted plant; therefore, deep tillage is not required.

kikuyu: Ūharagīria atīa harīa urathamīria mīungūrwa?
english: How do I prepare land for transplanting of cabbages seedlings?

kikuyu: Cimba na ūhure hianyū wūigananie na weherie ria na mahuti mothe
english: Plough and harrow the field until the soil is fine, level and free of weeds and plant debris.

kikuyu: Thondeka tuta na theci na ūkare mīkaro ya 20cm hīndi ya riūa na 30cm hīndi ya mbura
english: Form the bed with a plow by opening furrows to a depth of 20 cm during the dry season or at least 30 cm during the wet season

kikuyu: Nī makinya marīkū wagīrīirwo kūrūmīrīra ūgīthondeka tuta?
english: What are the steps for nursery establishment?

kikuyu: Thondeka tuta ya uraihu wa mita īmwe na wariī kuringana na mūigana wa mbegū ciaku
english: Prepare a seedbed of 1 m width and of a convenient length.

kikuyu: Rekia mbeū tūrima-īni ucoke uthike na gatīri kanini
english: Thinly sow the seeds in the drills and cover lightly with soil.

kikuyu: Īka īmwe ībatiī kūhandwo ngiramu 100-120 kūringana na muthemba(F1/OP) na ūrīa watigithūkania
english: The seed rate is about 100-120 g/īka (depending on variety (F1/OP) and spacing).

kikuyu: Ūmenyagīrīra mboga atīa irī tuta-inī?
english: What are the management practices in cabbage nurseries?

kikuyu: Itīīrīria maaī maiganu thutha-inī wa gūthamia kuuma tuta-inī.
english: Water thoroughly after transplanting and regularly.

kikuyu: Ona kūrī ūguo rī menyerera gūīkīra maaī maingī ndūkabuthie mīmera
english: However, avoid over-watering which can lead to “Damping-off” disease.

kikuyu: Tuta ya kūmbwo īgūrū nīya bata atia harī kūmenyerera mīmera?
english: Why are raised beds important in nursery management?

kikuyu: Tuta ya kūmbwo īgūrū nīnjega harī mīrita ya mīūngūrwa na gūte maaī
english: Raised beds recommended for root development and proper drainages

kikuyu: Tuta ya warie wa mita imwe na ūraihu ūtakīrītie mita igana rīmwe na ūriku wa sentimita ikūmi na ithano
english: • Bed width of 1 meter and a convenient length not exceeding 100 meters and a height of 15 centimeter

kikuyu: Tuta ya kūhura kabici īharagīrio atīa?
english: How is a cabbage nursery bed prepared?

kikuyu: Tuta yagīrīirwo nīgukorwo na ūriku wa 5-15 cm na warie wa mita īmwe
english: Seedbed is prepared approximately 5 - 15 cm high and 1.0 m wide.

kikuyu: Ongerera thumu mūhīu mūnini īgūrū ūcoke warīre na mahuti ma mūcere
english: Apply a thin layer of compost on the seedbed before mulching (with rice straw).

kikuyu: Natharī ya mita imwe o mwena, hūthira gramu 40 cia ammonium sulfate, gramu 50 cia super phosphate, gramu 30 cia potassium Chloride n kilo igirī cia thumu wa mahuti.
english: In a square meter seedbed, incorporate 40 g ammonium sulfate, 50 g super phosphate, 30 g potassium chloride, and 2 kg/ com post.

kikuyu: īkira neti ya kīruru tuta-inī nīguo kūgitīra mīūngūrwa kūrīo nī tūtambi, gūkuo nīkīguū kana gūcinwo nīriūa
english: Protect the seedbed with a net or shed to prevent the seedlings from early pest infestation, heavy rain, and direct sunlight.

kikuyu: Mboga yongagīrīra kī mīrīini itū?
english: What is the main nutrition importance of cabbage?

kikuyu: Kabici ikoraguo na Calcium, Iron, Vitamin A, C & E, Minerals, Riboflavin, Nicotinamine na Ascorbic Acid.
english: Contains Calcium, Iron, Vitamin A, C & E, Minerals, Riboflavin, Nicotinamine and Ascorbic Acid.

kikuyu: mboga nīteithagia gūthambia nda na mara īngīrīo īrīnjīthī na ītarī cumbī tondū nīirī na sulphur na chlorine
english: Cabbage has cleansing effect of stomach and intestinal tract if consumed raw without salt due to high sulphur and chlorine content

kikuyu: Kabici no īrīo ītarī nduge, īrugītwo, īcamūkītio kana ītukanītio thīinī wa indo ingī.
english: Cabbage is used as vegetables can be eaten raw, cooked, boiled, stuffed and sauerkraut.

kikuyu: Mahuti macio nī irio njega cia ng'ombe
english: The field byproducts are good source of animal feeds.

kikuyu: Nī maūguni marīkū maumanaga na kūrīa mboga?
english: What are the advantages of consuming cabbages?

kikuyu: Kabici ikoragwo na maguta ma mūtararīko marīa mamiheyaga mūtararīko wīkūraine na mūcamo.
english: Cabbage contains mustard oil that give them distinctive odor and taste.

kikuyu: Bamīrī ya mboga (kabici, broccoli, cauliflower na ingī) nīiteithagia kūgīrīrīria mūrimū wa cancer ya mara ona ya ngothi, nyondo, nda, bladder, ini na mahūri
english: Crucifers (cabbage, broccoli, cauliflower, etc) are particularly effective against colon cancer and also protect against cancers of the skin, breast, stomach, bladder, liver and lung;

kikuyu: Angikorwo gūtirī na matigari ma dawa cia kūraga tūtambi
english: provided there are not much pesticide residues.

kikuyu: Nī tūtambi tūrīkū tūgūmagīra mboga mūno Kenya?
english: What are the major pests that affect cabbage in Kenya?

kikuyu: Diamondback Moth (DBM), Sawfly cia mboga, ūme, Ndinoho na tūtengūri
english: Diamondback Moth (DBM),Cabbage Sawfly,Aphids Slugs Cutworms

kikuyu: ūngīmenya atīa atī kīhuruta nī mūthemba wa Diamond back?
english: How to identify diamond back ?

kikuyu: Matumbī marekagio igūrū rīa mathangū (Kīhuruta kīmwe kīa nga no kīrekie matumbī magana mana)
english: Eggs laid on upper surface of leaves (one female can lay 400 eggs).

kikuyu: Namba ino īingīhaga haria hanyoroku thī wa mahuti na nī nyingī makīria icīgoini cia ūrugarī
english: Pupation takes place into a silken gauze-like cocoon at underside of leaf.Infestations are normally serious in drier months.

kikuyu: Kīhuruta kīa diamond black kīngīgirīrīrio atīa kabici-inī?
english: How is diamondback moth controlled in cabbage?

kikuyu: Hūthīra dawa cia tūtambi ta Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) (DELFIN 6.4W.G® and HALT 50WP®).
english: Use of bio-insecticides such as Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) (DELFIN 6.4W.G® and HALT 50WP®).

kikuyu: Kūhandanīria na mīmera mūthemba ūngī ūrīa ūteithagia kūingata tūtambi (ta nyanya) kana mīmera īrīa īhūthagīrwo ta mūtego (Indian Mustard) nīīnyihagia gūthūkio kwa mboga nī DBM .
english: Intercropping with other crops which act as repellants (e.g. Tomato) or trap crops (e.g. Indian Mustard) reduces DBM destruction on Cabbage.

kikuyu: Rīrīa nyanya īkūhūthīka kūingata tūtambi, kabici ibatiī kuhandwo thikū 30 thutha wa nyanya kūhandwo.
english: When Tomato is used as a repellent, Cabbage is planted 30 days after Tomato.

kikuyu: Hūthīra tūng'ang'i mūthemba wa igi(Diadegma spp) kana dawa īthondeketwo kuuma mūtī-inī wa mūthandū ta azadirachtin (Neemraj Super 3000®) etc.
english: Use of parasitic wasp (Diadegma spp.).Use of neem products, such as azadirachtin (Neemraj Super 3000®) etc.

kikuyu: Kīgunyū kīagimara gītuīkaga kīgi kīna gīthūri kīirū na nda ya rangi mūcamu wa ngoikoni.
english: Adult is a wasp with dark thorax and blight yellow abdomen.

kikuyu: Matumbī marekagio marekanītie ithagū-inī.
english: Eggs laid singly inside the leaf.

kikuyu: kīana gīa kīgunyū kīgūaga tīīri-inī kīngīthīnio hanini. Gīkūragīra tīīri-inī
english: Larvae drop to the ground if there is slight disturbance.Pupation takes place inside the soil.

kikuyu: Ingīrigīrīria atīa sawfly mboga-inī
english: How to control cabbage sawfly?

kikuyu: Gūthūkangia kwa ria rīa barī ya Brassicaceae (famīrī cia kabici).
english: Destruction of wild plants of the Brassicaceae family.

kikuyu: Hūthīra dawa mīthemba ta Methoxyfenozide (RUNNER 240SC®)Imidacloprid (MURCLOPRID 25 WP®).Trichlorfon (DIPTEREX 95 SP®)
english: Use of Methoxyfenozide (RUNNER 240SC®)Imidacloprid (MURCLOPRID 25 WP®).Trichlorfon (DIPTEREX 95 SP®)

kikuyu: Nī mītheba īrīkū ya ūme īgūmagīra mboga?
english: What types of aphid affect cabbage?

kikuyu: ūngīmenya ūme wa Mealy mboga-inī atīa?
english: How to identify a mealy cabbage aphid?

kikuyu: cikoragwo na rangi mūthitu wa ngirini na ūkahumbīrwo nīrūkūngū rūnini rwa mealy.
english: They are pale green and usually covered with a light dust of mealy powder.

kikuyu: Kūgūmīrwo nīūme gūcūngagīrīra gwīkūja na gūthūka kwa mathagū namo maumīrīra nī ciongo ciīkūnjite ūūru
english: Aphid attack results in curled and distorted leaves which in turn leads to poor head formation.

kikuyu: Ingīgirīrīria atīa ūme wa mealybug kabici-inī?
english: How to control mealybug cabbage aphid?

kikuyu: ūngīmenya atīa Ndinoho mboga-inī
english: How to identify slug in cabbage?

kikuyu: Ingīgirīrīria atīa ndinoho kabici-inī
english: How to control slugs in cabbage?

kikuyu: Rūmīrīra njīra cia kīmerera ta gūikia ndinoho maaĩ-inī(thika tūmīkebe tīīri-inī wīiyūrītie na maaĩ) na kwongerera dawa ya kūgucīrīria ndinoho.
english: Cultural control by drowning the slugs in water (bury tins at ground level and fill with water) and add yeast to attract the slugs

kikuyu: ūngĩmenya atĩa kīgunyū gī kabici-ini?
english: How to identify cut worm in cabbages?

kikuyu: Nī igunyū cia rangi wa grey iria ciguraragīa kana kūrenga mūkori gītina-inī gūcūngīrīria mūmera kūgūa
english: They are grayish black larvae that partially or completely bite the stem at ground level causing the plant to fall over.

kikuyu: Kaingī cikoragwo ciīhithīte tīri-inī hakuhī na mūngūrwa
english: They are often found hiding in soil near the cut seedlings

kikuyu: Ingīrūgamia atīa ūme mboga-inī
english: How to control cutworm in cabbage?

kikuyu: Na njira ya kūruta na moko nīgūkorwo gatambi gaka nīkonekaga na ūhūthū mumera-inī mūthūkangie na mūno kīambīrīria-inī gīa kūgūmīrwo
english: Hand removal since the pest is easily found near the damaged plant, especially at the beginning of infestation.

kikuyu: Kūrīmīra mboga tene nīgūthūkangagia gīikaro gīa kūrekeria matumbī
english: Early weeding destroys sites for egg laying.

kikuyu: Kūrīma kūguūragia tutambī kūrī thūū ciako na kūhotomio nī riūa
english: Ploughing exposes the pest to its predators and desiccation.

kikuyu: Nī mīrimū īrīku kaingī yonekanaga kabici-inī?
english: What are the major cabbage diseases in Kenya?

kikuyu: Damping-off,Bacterial Black Rot,Black Leg (Dry Rot Canker),Ring Spot,Alternaria Leaf Spot,Bacterial Soft Rot,Club Root
english: Damping-off,Bacterial Black Rot,Black Leg (Dry Rot Canker),Ring Spot,Alternaria Leaf Spot,Bacterial Soft Rot,Club Root

kikuyu: Mūrimū ūyū ūrehagwo nī fungi.
english: The disease is caused by the fungi

kikuyu: Nī moritū marīkū monekaga kaingī tuta-inī
english: • Common problem at the nursery stage

kikuyu: No kūhoteke ūingīhe mūno hīndī ya mbura
english: • More likely prevalent during rainy season

kikuyu: Kūgīa na ūgunyū mūingī mūno nīgūgūtūma mbegū igwatwo nī mūrimū
english: • Too much moisture will dispose the crop to the disease.

kikuyu: Wīītheme guitīīrīria maaī maingī na bataraitha gūkīra gīthimi na mūno makīria iria cīīna nitrates
english: Avoid excessive watering and fertilization, particularly with nitrates

kikuyu: Wīītheme mīgūnda yanakorwo na mīrimū
english: • Avoid fields with a history of the disease

kikuyu: kūmenya kugarūrīra mīgūnda
english: • Practice crop rotation

kikuyu: Nī mīthemba īrīkū ya kahūa īkūragio gūkū Kenya?
english: Which varieties of coffee are grown in the Kenya?

kikuyu: SL 34 īrīa īhandagūo kūndū kūrīa kūrī irīma; SL 28 īhandagūo na ūtaganu wa fiti kenda gwa kenda na yagīrīire kūhandwo kūndū kūrīa kūrī irīma, īkoragwo na mīri mīega, īgīaga na magetha maingī no nīinyitagwo nī mīrimū raithi.
english: SL 34 suitable for high altitude area;SL 28 at a spacing of 9ft by 9ft suitable for medium to high altitude area, has good rooting system, high yielder but susceptible to diseases.

kikuyu: K7 nīyagīraga kūndū kūrīa gūtarī igūrū mūno, īkoragwo na mīri mīega, īciaraga mūno noo nīīnyitagwo nī mīrimū raithi.
english: K7 suitable for low altitude area, has good rooting system, high yielder but susceptible to diseases.

kikuyu: Batian nī mūthemba ūrīa mūerū mūno būrūri-inī ūyū, nīūhandagwo kūndū guothe kūrīa gūkūragio kahūa Kenya, nīūciaraga mūno, nīūhandagwo itina nyingī harī īka, nīūhotaga gūitiria mīrimū na nīngīūkoragwo na mīri ītambaga kūndū kūnene.
english: Batian is the newest variety in the country, is suited to all coffee growing zones in Kenya, a high yielder, has good population per unit, moderate disease tolerance but with moderate rooting system.

kikuyu: Itina cia kahūa ciagīrīirwo gūtaganūkanio atia hīndī ya kūhanda?
english: Which is the recommended spacing for coffee?

kikuyu: Mīthemba ngūrani ya kahūa īhandagwo na ithimo ngūrani
english: Different varieties require different spacings.

kikuyu: Mūthemba wa Ruiru 11 wagīrīire ūtaganu wa fiti 6 kwa 6 na nīūrīmaciaro maingī oharī gītina, ūhandagwo itina nyingī harī īka, nī wītiragia mīrimū no mīri ndītheremaga wega. Batian yendaga ūtiganu wa fiti mūgwanja kwa inyanya.
english: Ruiru 11 spacing of 6ft by 6ft. It is a high yielder, has best population per unit, high disease tolerance but with poor rooting system.Batian is at a spacing of 7ft by 8ft.

kikuyu: Mīthemba īrīa mīega ya kūhanda īcagūragwo kūringa na rīera rīa matūra na tīīri.
english: The best variety to plant will depend on the zone as different varieties are suited for different ecological zones.

kikuyu: Mīthemba īngī ya kahūa īrīa īhandagwo mūno nī SL-28, SL- 34, K7, Ruiru 11, na Batian.
english: Other coffee varieties commonly grown are SL-28, SL-34, K7, Ruiru 11 and Batian.

kikuyu: Hihi mūthemba wa SL nī ūrīkū?
english: What is SL variety?

kikuyu: SL nī mūthemba wa kahūa ūrīa ūkūraga wega kūndū gūtarī irīma nene kana mīaragano-inī.
english: SL is a coffee variety suitable for middle altitudes.

kikuyu: Mūthemba ūyū wītagwo SL kuumana na kīhumo kīagwo kīrīa nī Scott Laboratories, īrīa ūmūthī yūīkaine ta Kabete Kenya.
english: It's known as SL since it was selected in former Scott Laboratories- Now Kabete,Kenya.

kikuyu: Mūthemba ūyū nī mūraihu ūndū ūrīa ūtūmaga ūhote kūrīa irio nyingī kuuma tīīrī-inī kwa wīingī.
english: The strain has a long stem which is suitable for absorbing more nutrients from the soil.

kikuyu: SL 28 yacagūrirwo kuuma mūgūnda-inī wa Scott Laboratories īrīa rīū niyo National Agricultural Laboratories, NARL Kabete na waciarithanirio kuuma kūrī mūthemba ūngī warutītwo Tanzania ya rūgongo mwaka-inī wa 1931 ūrīa ūrī ūhoti wa gūītiria wagi wa maaī.
english: The SL 28 cultivar was selected at the former Scott Laboratories (now the National Agricultural Laboratories, NARL situated at Kabete) on a single tree basis from the Tanganyika Drought Resistant variety selected in Northern Tanzania in 1931.

kikuyu: Mūthemba wa SL 34 onagwo waciarithanīirio mūgūnda-inīo ūyū wa Scott Laboratories kuuma mūthemba wa Faranja.
english: SL 34 was also selected at the former Scott Laboratories from French Mission Coffee.

kikuyu: Kahūa gaka gaciaraga wega kūndū igurū kana irīma-inī na kūndū kūrī mbura nyingī.
english: The cultivar is adapted to high altitude areas with good rainfall.

kikuyu: Mūthemba ūyū wīkūranite nīūndū nīūrī mathangū marī rangi wa gītīri gīcamu na ngirini.
english: It is majorly characterized by dark bronze shoot tipped plants with a few green-tipped strains.

kikuyu: Ruiru 11 nī mūthemba ūrikū wa kahūa?
english: What is Ruiru 11 variety?

kikuyu: Ruiru 11 yarekereirio mwaka-inī wa 1985, na wetanītio na kūrīa wathundūrīirwo, Kenya Coffee Research Station.
english: Ruiru 11 variety was released in 1985. The variety name has the prefix “Ruiru” referring to the location of the Kenyan Coffee Research Station where the variety was developed.

kikuyu: Rītwa rīrī rīrūmīrīirwo nī namba ikūmi na īmwe.
english: The name is completed by an additional two code numbers, 11.

kikuyu: Mūthemba ūyū nīūhotaga gwītiria mīrimū ya CBD na CRL na nīngī mbegū ciagwo ikoragwo irīnyitu ikahothia mūrīmi kūona magetha maingī, makīria kūndū kūrīa gekaga wega na kūrīa itina nyingī ihandītwo o īka. kwoguo kahūa gagakorwo na ūhūrani wa mwanya gakīringithanio na mīmera īrīa īngī.
english: The variety is not only resistant to CBD and CLR but is also compact allowing farmers to intensity production per unit land especially in high potential areas where population is high and coffee is in competition with other crops and farm enterprises required for food security and income.

kikuyu: Ruiru 11 yagīrīirwo kūhandwo gatagatī ka mīmera ngiri igīrī īmwe na magana matano nginya ngiri ithatū na magana matatū hectare-inī īmwe ūkiringithania na mītī ngiri imwe na magana matatū ya kahua mīthemba ya kīmerera.
english: Ruiru 11 is planted at a density of 2500/3300 trees/ha compared to 1300 trees/ha for the traditional varieties.

kikuyu: Ningīkoyaga ihinda inini gūkūra na kwoguo mūrīmi akagīa magetha tene na akajia kūgūnīka.
english: The variety comes into production earlier, hence earlier realization of benefits to the farmers.

kikuyu: Rūirū 11 rīrīa yathondekagwo, nīgwatigīrīirwo atī mūcamo nī wagīkīro kīa igūrū ota ūrīa thoko yendaga.
english: The development of Ruiru 11 also took into consideration the importance of quality as a major marketing parameter.

kikuyu: Na rīu tondū kahūa ga kīmerera nī kamenyeretwo nīanyui kenya, Ruiru 11 yathondekirwo na mūcamo ūhanaine na wa kahūa ga kīmerera
english: Since the quality of the traditional varieties was already popular among consumers of Kenyan coffee, Ruiru 11 was developed with quality attributes similar to the traditional varieties.

kikuyu: Itina cia kahūa gaka onacio nīitumanagio rīrīa ikūhandwo.
english: It's also compact. therefore, more stems can be accommodated per unit area.

kikuyu: Nī mūthemba ūrīkū wa kahūa ūkūraga wega kūndū kwīna irīma?
english: Which type of coffee grows well in high altitude zones?

kikuyu: Ruiru 11 nī mūthemba ūngīkūra wega kūndū o guothe kūhandagwo kahūa
english: Ruiru 11 can also be grown in all coffee growing areas

kikuyu: Ngūrani ya Ruiru 11 na Batian nī īrīkū?
english: What is the difference between Ruiru 11 and Batian?

kikuyu: Ruiru 11 nī mūthemba ūkūraga kūndū guothe kahūa gakūragio na itina itaganagio na fiti ithathatū gwa ithathatū.
english: Ruiru 11 is suited to all coffee growing zones in Kenya at a spacing of 6ft by 6ft.

kikuyu: Batian naguo nī mūthemba mwerū mūno Kenya na nīūrakūra wega kūndū guothe kūhandagwo kahūa na ūhandagwo na ūtaganu wa fiti mūgwanja kwa inyanya.
english: Batian is the newest variety in Kenya and it is suited to all coffee growing zones in Kenya at a spacing of 7ft by 8ft.

kikuyu: Ingīgūra mbegū kana mīūngūrwa ya kahūa kū?
english: Where to buy coffee seeds and seedlings?

kikuyu: Mbegū irīa ikinyanīirie ikīro cionekaga CRI Ruiru.
english: Certified seed is only available from CRI-Ruiru centre.

kikuyu: Ūthure mīūngūrwa īna ūraihu wa sentimita mīrongo ītatu nginya mīrongo īna na īkorwo na kahonge kamwe kana twīīrī twīnahinya.
english: Select seedlings that are about 30 - 40 cm tall, with 1 - 2 pairs of primary branches and that should have undergone sufficient hardening

kikuyu: Kahūa mūthemba wa Robusta ūkūragio kū kenya?
english: Where is Robusta coffee grown in Kenya?

kikuyu: kahūa mūthemba wa Robusta ūkūragio thīinī wa county ithano iria nī Kisumu,Homabay, Siaya, Bungoma na Busia.Kwīna ūhotekū wa mūthemba ūyū wa kahūa ūkorwo ūgīkūrio Kilifi na Kwale gīchūa-inī.
english: Robusta coffee is currently grown in 5 counties (Kisumu, Homabay, Siaya, Bungoma and Busia) with a potential of expansion to Kilifi and Kwale counties in the coastal region.

kikuyu: O ūrīa ūrambata irīma-inī, noguo rīera rīcenjagia na makīria uhehu ūkaingīha. ūndū ūyū nīūtūmaga kahūa gakorwo na ngūrani na mūcamo ūgacenjia.
english: The altitude is closely related to the latitude of the region which affects the temperature, and this directly affects the quality of the coffee bean.

kikuyu: Nīūndū wa rīera kūheha, mbegū nīcioyaga kahinda karaihu gūkūra na kuoguo igakorwo irī nyitu, igakorwo na mūcinīre ūiganarīirie na gīkombe gīako gīgakorwo na mūcamo mwega.
english: When grown in lower temperatures, the beans take longer to develop, resulting in more complex and delicious flavors. This creates denser beans that roast more evenly and produces a better cup of coffee.

kikuyu: Mūthemba wa Ruiru 11 woyaga kahinda kaigana atia kūruta maciaro ma mbere?
english: How long does Ruiru 11 coffee take to mature?

kikuyu: Mūthemba ūyū wa kahūa ka Ruiru 11 nīūkūraga narua ūkīringithanio na mīthemba īyo īngī tondū ūrūtaga maciaro ma mbere thutha wa kahinda ka mīaka īrī.
english: Compared with other varieties, which are more slow-growing, Ruiru 11 generally produces its first harvest within two years of planting.

kikuyu: Gītina kīmwe gīa kahūa kiagīrīire gūciara kilo cigana?
english: How many kgs can one coffee tree produce?

kikuyu: Gūciara gwa kahūa kūringanaga na mūthemba wa kahūa ,rīera rīa itūra, mūtungatīre, gatagatī ka mangī maingī.
english: The yield per tree depends on the variety, ecological factors, agronomic practices among others.

kikuyu: Kaingī, mūtī ūmwe wa kahūa ūciaraga kiro igīrī na nuthu o mwaka iria nī nuthu kiro ya kahūa ka green kana ngiramu 400 ma kahūa gacine karīa kangīthondeka ikombe mīrongo īna cia kahūa.
english: Generally, Coffee trees produce an average of 2.5kg of berries per year, yielding around 0.5kg of green coffee or the equivalent of 0.4kg of roasted coffee, which corresponds to about 40 cups of beverage

kikuyu: Mīūngūrūa ya kahūa ka Ruiru 11 yendagio ata?
english: How much is Ruiru 11 coffee seedlings in Kenya?

kikuyu: Kahūa gakūraga wega kūndū gūtarī kūhio mūno, kūhehu no ūrugarī mūnini na tīīri mūnoru.
english: The optimal coffee-growing conditions include cool to warm tropical climates, rich soils.

kikuyu: Natharī ya kahūa īthondekagwo atīa ?
english: How to make a nursery bed for coffee?

kikuyu: Harīria handū harī na wariī wa fiti inya na ūraihu wa fiti ikūmi (tukania thumu wa ng'ombe na tīīri mūirū kwa icūnje 1 gwa 10). Enja marima matarī mariku mūno na ūhande mbegū cia kahūa. Itīīrīria maaī na ūhumbīre na mahuti.
english: Prepare 4ft (wide) x 10ft (long) beds. Mix 1 (composted bio-slurry) : 10 (black loam soil). Plant the coffee beans at shallow depth. Water the beds, then mulch

kikuyu: Ingīhota atīa gūtungata natharī ya kahūa?
english: How do I raise coffee nursery?

kikuyu: Kūharīria natharī ya kahūa kūbataraga handū hena wariī, haraganū na hena tīīri mūnoru.
english: Preparing the nursery plot. Choose a bigger, flat and fertile plot next to the seed plot.

kikuyu: Thondeka natharī cia wariī wa mita 1.2 ugītigaga tūcīra twa sentimita 60 gatagatī gacio.
english: Make beds of soil 1.2 metres wide, with 60-centimetre paths in between.

kikuyu: Tūngītūngata atia mīūngūrwa ya kahūa ī natharī-inī?
english: How to take care of coffee seedlings in a nursery?

kikuyu: Gūra mīūngūrwa kuuma kambuni iria iramenyeka nīgūo ūkorwo na ūma wamūkūrire wacio. Gūra tu kuuma kwa Coffee Research Institute
english: Use planting materials from known sources to ascertain genetic purity. Source seed ONLY from the coffee research institute .

kikuyu: Mūtukanio wa harīa mīūngūrwa īkūhandwo hatigakorwo na indo cia gūthūkia ta tūtambi kama thumu.
english: The Potting mixture should be free from either biological or chemical contaminants.

kikuyu: īkīra kīruru kīa ūraihu wa mita 1.2 kana futi 4 na ūtumanie thikū cia mbere.
english: Put a shade at 1.2 m (4 ft) above the poly bed • Provide dense shade initially •

kikuyu: Ehereria kīruru kahorakahora nīgūo komīrīrie.
english: Harden seedlings by gradually reducing the shade.

kikuyu: Eheria kīruru gīothe mweri ūmwe mbere ya gūgatwara kūhanda mūgūnda.
english: Remove shade completely one month before transplanting.

kikuyu: Tūmīra dawa cia tūtabi na mīrimū iria hetūkīe.
english: Use ONLY recommended pesticides to control pests and diseases.

kikuyu: Mīūngūrwa ya kahūa īrutagwo natharī-inī rī?
english: When coffee seedling moved to the nursery?

kikuyu: Mbegū ya kahūa yumīraga wiki ithathatū kuuma mūthi ūria yahurirwo.
english: Six weeks after sowing, the little plant comes up from the soil.

kikuyu: Thutha wa mīeri itatū, mathangū meerī ma mbere magakorwo methondekete wega.
english: When the seedlings are three months old, the first two leaves are well developed.

kikuyu: Rīrī nīrīo ihinda rīega rīa gūthamia mīūngūrwa yaku na gūtwara natharī-inī.
english: This is the moment to take the seedlings out of the seed beds and to transplant them into a nursery.

kikuyu: Ūgīthamia mīūngūrwa yaku ūmenyerere ndūkaunange mīri.
english: In removing the seedlings from the seed beds, be very careful not to break the roots

kikuyu: Mīūgūrwa ya kahūa īikaraga natharī-inī ihinda rīigana atīa?
english: How long does the coffee seedlings stay in a nursery?

kikuyu: Ūgīthamia mīūngūrwa kuuma natharī-inī ūgītwara mūgūnda menyerera kuunanga mīri.
english: When you remove the coffee tree seedlings from the nursery bed in order to plant them in the plantation, be very careful not to break the roots.

kikuyu: Nī njīra irīkū njega cia gūciarithania kahūa?
english: What is the best method for propagating coffee plants?

kikuyu: Thuura thuna ciothe nūngarū cia ūraihu wa iji inyanya nginya ikūmi na ūmībure ūgītigagīa mathangū merī.
english: Select a straight shoot that's about 8 to 10 inches long and remove all but a pair of upper leaves.

kikuyu: Ūcoke ūhande thīinī wa tūnyūngū na ūige tīīri na ūgūnyu mūnini.
english: Then, plant the cutting in a small pot of soilless potting mix, and keep the soil slightly moist.

kikuyu: Ūngīgeria kūgūcia mīūngūrwa naigūru taarī kūmunya, wīigue nī mūnyitu, ūmenye mīri nīyanjītie gūikīra.
english: When you can gently tug on the plant and feel resistance, you'll know roots have formed.

kikuyu: Tinia thuna ya ūraihu wa iji ithathatū na īkorwo na mathangū meerī.
english: The cutting should be about 6 inches long with at least two leaves.

kikuyu: Ūcoke ūtinie gītina wūinamītie
english: Snip off the stem with a diagonal cut.

kikuyu: Gīkīro gia kana: Ūcoke ūbure mathangū kuuma nathī ūgītigagia manini.
english: Step 4: Remove the leaves from the bottom third of the cutting.

kikuyu: Ikia thuna yaku dawa-inī ya guteng'eria mīīri ūcoke ūhande irima-inī.
english: Dip the cut end in rooting hormone, then plant the cutting in the hole

kikuyu: Kahūa gaciarithanagio atīa?
english: How is coffee propagated?

kikuyu: Wagīrīirwo gūthamia mīūngūrūa ya kahūa atīa kuuma nathari-inī ūgītwara mūgūnda-inī?
english: How do you transplant the coffee seedlings to the farm?

kikuyu: Hariīia mūgūnda na njīra ya kūrīma na wīkire thumu wa mahiū kana wa mabūthū ma mahuti nīgūo wongerere ūnorū wa tiri ūcio.
english: Prepare the new planting site by loosening the soil and adding compost or other organic matter to improve the soil structure and fertility.

kikuyu: Handa handū hakinyagīrwo nī riūa wega na hatangīaraha maaī.
english: Choose a location that receives plenty of sunlight and has well-drained soil.

kikuyu: Mīūngūrwa yarīkia kūharīrio, enja irima inene rīkūiganīra mīīri wega ūndū ītekūhatīkana.
english: When the seedlings are ready, dig a large enough hole to accommodate the seedling’s root system without crowding it.

kikuyu: Mīthike ugīkindagīra tīīri kahora kahora nīgūo kūruta rīera rīria rīngikorwo thīinī.
english: Fill in the hole around the roots, and firm the soil gently to remove any air pockets.

kikuyu: Kahūa karabataraga maūndū marīkū nīgetha gakūre wega?
english: What are the conditions for coffee growing?

kikuyu: Wagīrīirwo nīkūrora maūndū marīkū ūgīthura mūgūnda wa kūhanda kahūa?
english: What to consider when selecting a site for coffee planting?

kikuyu: tīīri wagīrīirwo nīgūkorwo na mūmbīre mwega nīguo kūhotithia mīri ya kahūa gūtonya wega. Ūū nīūndū mītī ya kahūa īkoragwo na mīri ya itimū.
english: The soil must have a good structure so that the roots can penetrate well.This is because coffee trees have tap roots.

kikuyu: Mīri īno ya itimū īmeraga irūngarīte na gwūikūrūka haraya thīinī wa tīīri.
english: The tap root goes straight down into the soil.

kikuyu: No wagīrie mūūmbīre wa tīīri na njīra ya gwīkīra thumu itina-inī cia mītī ya kahūa.
english: You can improve the soil structure by spreading manure around the base of the coffee trees.

kikuyu: No mūhaka tīīri ūkorwo mūriku nīguo mīri īhote kwīngīra handū haraya. Ndūka hande kahūa handū harī na tīīri mūnyitu, na wakorwo no mūhaka, nīwega kūhaciba.
english: The soil must be deep, so that the roots can go down deep. Never plant coffee trees in soil which has a hard layer, or, if you do, break up the hard layer

kikuyu: Mūgūnda wa kūhanda kahūa ūharagīrīo atia?
english: How to prepare land for planting coffee?

kikuyu: Mūgūnda ūharagīrio mīeri ītandatū mbere ya kūhanda, weherie mahuti, ithukī na mīri yothe.
english: Land preparation should be done early about 6 months prior to planting by clearing existing vegetation and getting rid of tree stumps and roots.

kikuyu: Angīkorwo mūgūnda wīna mītī mīingī, hebata kūmīeheria mwaka ūmwe mbere ya kūhanda kahūa.
english: If the farm is heavily forested gradually dry existing trees about a year before planting.

kikuyu: Mūgūnda ūtaninīte mīeri ītandatū ndūbatiī kūhandwo kahūa nīūndū wa ūgwati wa mūrimū wa Armillaria ūrīa ūtūmaga mīri ībuthe.
english: Land cleared of trees within 6 months should not be used for coffee planting because of the risk of Armillaria, a fungal disease that causes root rot.

kikuyu: Tigīrīra tīīri nī mūthime nīguo ūmenyeke ūria ūhana.
english: Ensure soil analysis is done to determine the inherent soil condition.

kikuyu: Gitīra beji na njīra ya kūhanda nyeki ta mūthemba wa Blue grass (Paspulum notatum) mīthia-inī.
english: Protect bench terraces by planting grasses e.g. Blue grass (Paspulum notatum) on the bench faces

kikuyu: Nī njīra īrīkū njega makīria ya gūkūria kahūa?
english: What is the best way to grow coffee?

kikuyu: Tiga ūtaganu wa mita ithatū kuuma gītina gia kahūa nginya kīria kīngī. Kwa njīra ino,no ūhande itina ngiri īmwe harī hectare īmwe ya mūgūnda.
english: Leave 3 metres between trees. In this way you can plant about 1 000 coffee trees per hectare.

kikuyu: Mbere ya kūhanda mīūngūrūa, enja marima na ūtūkanie tīīri mīeri īrī mbere ya kūhanda.
english: Before planting the coffee seedlings you must dig holes in order to stir the soil and loosen it. Dig the holes two months before planting the coffee trees.

kikuyu: Mīūngūrwa ya kahūa yagīrīire kūhandwo atīa?
english: How to plant coffee seedlings?

kikuyu: Mbere ya kūhanda, mbegu ciagīire kūrindwo maai-inī mathaa 24 nīguo ihūthie ngothi na imere na ihenya
english: Before planting, the seeds should be soaked in water for 24 hours to soften the seed coat and encourage germination.

kikuyu: Kahūa kagīrīire gūtigithūkanio atīa hīndī ya kūhanda?
english: What is the recommended spacing of coffee?

kikuyu: Nī tīīri ūrīkū mwega wa kūhanda kahūa?
english: Which is the best type of soil to plant coffee?

kikuyu: Kahūa nogakūre tīīri-inī ūtiganīte no ūrīa mwega mūno nī tīīri ūrīa wīna ūnoru, mūtune kana volcanic red soil, na sandy-loam.
english: Coffee can be grown on many different soil types, but the ideal is a fertile, volcanic red earth or a deep, sandy loam.

kikuyu: Ūrūrū mwega wa tīīri wa kūhanda kahūa nī ūrīkū?
english: What is the soil pH for coffee cultivation?

kikuyu: Kahūa kagīraga tīīri-inī ūrī na ūrūrū wa gatagatī wa gīthimo gia pH gia kuuma ithano nginya ithathatū.
english: Coffee prefers a soil with pH of 5 to 6.

kikuyu: Nīwega kūinamia gītina gīa kahūa nīguo kīrute honge nyingī?
english: Is it advisable to bend newly transplanted coffee to produce more branches?

kikuyu: Wagīrīirwo gūtinia gītina kīambere nīguo kīrute honge ingī nyingī na irīna hinya.
english: Newly planted should be cut within the first two primaries to allow strong double shooting

kikuyu: Kahūa mīthemba ya SL34, SL28 na K7 yaragīrīirwo gūtigithūkanio atīa īkīhandwo?
english: What is the recommended spacing SL 34, SL 28, and K7 coffee seedlings varieties?

kikuyu: Mīthemba ya SL 34,SL28, and K7 yagīrīirwo nī ūtaganu wa mita 2.74 gwa 2.74 kana (futi 9 gwa 9).
english: SL 34, SL 28, and K7 varieties, the spacing should be 2.74m x 2.74m (9ft × 9ft).

kikuyu: īka imwe ībatiī kūhandwo itina cigana cia kahūa?
english: How many coffee trees can be planted in an īka?

kikuyu: Itina ngiri īmwe na magana matatū ma mīrongo īnana nginya ngiri igīrī cia mūthemba wa Arabica kana itina magana meerī ma mīrongo ītano na ithatū nginya magana matandatū ma mīrongo mūgwanja na ithano cia mūthemba wa Robusta.
english: 1380-2000 trees per īka depending on the arabica variety; in the case of Robusta, plant between 253-675 trees per īka

kikuyu: Wagīrīire kūhanda itina cigana cia kahūa mūthemba wa Ruiru harī īka imwe ya mūgūnda?
english: How many Ruiru coffee trees per īka?

kikuyu: Mūthemba wa Ruiru II wagīrīire ūtaganu wa mita igīrī kwa igīrī kana futi ithathatū gwa ithathatū. Ūū nīkuga ūkūhanda itina ngiri igīrī na magana matano harī hectare īmwe kana ngiri imwe na ikūmi na igirī īka-inī īmwe.
english: Ruiru II requires a spacing of 2×2 meters (6.6 by 6.6 feet).

kikuyu: Ūū nīkuga ūkūhanda itina ngiri igīrī na magana matano harī hectare īmwe kana ngiri imwe na ikūmi na igirī īka-inī īmwe.
english: With this spacing, it will translate to 2,500 Ruiru II coffee trees per hectare (1,012 coffee plants per īka).

kikuyu: kahūa mūthemba wa Ruiru 11 kagīrīire kūhandwo na ūtaganu wa mita igīrī kwa igīrī kana futi 6.6 gwa 6.6.
english: Ruiru 11 variety, the spacing should be 2m x 2m (6.6 ft. x 6.6 ft.)

kikuyu: kahūa mūthemba wa Batian kagīrīirwo kūhandwo na ūtaganu wūigana atīa?
english: What is the recommended spacing of Batian coffee seedlings?

kikuyu: kahūa mūthemba wa Batian kagīrīire kūhandwo na ūtaganu wa mita 2.1 kwa 2.5 kana futi 7 kwa 8.
english: Batian variety, the spacing should be 2.1m x 2.5m (7ft x 8 ft.).

kikuyu: rīrīa ūkwenda kūgarūra kahūa, wagīrīire gūtiga gīthūkī kīna ūrahu woigana atīa?
english: When you want to change cycle, what height of stump should you leave?

kikuyu: Ceha honge gatagati ka ūraihu wa sentimita 25-30 kuuma thīna ūgītinagia na ango ya 45° ūrutītie na nja .
english: Cut stems about 25-30 cm from ground at angle of 45 degrees slanting outwards

kikuyu: Hihi mūcehere mwega wa kahūa gūkū Kenya nī ūrīkū?
english: How to prune coffee in Kenya?

kikuyu: ceha kahūa gaku mūtwe nīguo gatigakīrie ūraihu wa mita imwe na nuthu nginya mita igīrī.
english: Cut off the top of the tree so that the coffee tree is not taller than 1.5 to 2 metres.

kikuyu: Ruta honge iria irī gītina-inī.
english: Remove the branches at the bottom of the trunk.

kikuyu: Tigia honge iria ndungu na irī na riri.
english: Leave only the thickest and best branches on the trunk.

kikuyu: Tinia iria njeke na nini. Ruta honge iria nguo, iria ciumīte na iria ndwaru. Ruta thuna ciothe tondū itirī na bata.
english: Cut away all the small branches that grow on the trunk. Cut away all the small branches that grow on the trunk. Cut away all the dead and dry branches, and all diseased branches. Cut away suckers; they are not needed.

kikuyu: kahūa no gūcehwo karīo kanini na njīra ya gūkarenga kīongo nīgūo honge cia mwena ciitīkīre gūkūra na ihote kūruta mahūa na matunda maingī.
english: Coffee plants can be pruned in the early stages of growth by cutting back the growing tip to encourage lateral branching, this will promote more flowers and fruits.

kikuyu: Bata wa gūceha kahūa nī ūrīkū?
english: Why is it important to prune coffee trees?

kikuyu: Gūceha na kweheria honge ciothe cia kahūa iria ītarī na bata nīgūcokagia riri wako na gakahota kugīa na maciaro maingī.
english: Pruning and stumping help to improve the health and yield of your coffee plants.

kikuyu: kahūa karagīrwo mūceng'i atīa?
english: How to mulch coffee?

kikuyu: No ūhūthīre ngurura cia makongo ma mīrura, mahuti ma mīceho ya kahūa, mabebe kana macoya ma marigū.
english: It can be done using sisal waste, coffee pruning, and maize or banana trash.

kikuyu: Mūceng'i īrehaga baita nene, kwa mūhiano, gūteithīrīria kūiga maaī tīīri-inī rīrīa gwī kūūmū, kūgiria ria rīkūre, gūtuīka thumu rīrīa mahuti macio mabutha , gūthondeka mūmbīre wa tīīri ona kūgiria tīīri gūkuo nī kīguo, kūnyihia ūrugarī wa tīīri ona ningī nīūrigagīrīria tūtambi ta thrips gūtherema.
english: Mulching has several benefits to coffee e.g. conservation of moisture during dry spells, suppression of weed growth, nutrient supply, improvement of soil structure and water infiltration, checking of soil erosion and topsoil temperature as well as reduction of pests’ incidence, e.g. thrips.

kikuyu: kahūa kagimaraga thutha wa mīaka 4 nginya 7, nīrīo kambagia gūciara matunda honge-inī. Matunda maya nīmo metagwo cherries.
english: Coffee tree reaches maturity after 4 – 7 years, when it begins to bear fruit in clusters along its branches. These fruits are commonly referred to as cherries.

kikuyu: kahūa koyaga kahinda kaigana atīa nīgetha gakūre?
english: How long does coffee take to grow?

kikuyu: kahūa nogaikare gatagatī ka mīaka itatū nginya īna nīguo kambie gūciara matunda.
english: It can take anywhere between three to four years after planting for coffee plants to bear the cherries.

kikuyu: Kambaga kūruta mahūa meerū na thutha wa kahinda ta ka mīeri īnana, matunda makambīrīria kuoneka.
english: They start by producing white blossoms and around eight months later, coffee cherries will usually appear.

kikuyu: matunda maya nīmo makūīte mbegū iria ciūīkaine ta coffee beans
english: The cherries contain the coffee seeds or more commonly recognised as the coffee beans.

kikuyu: Kamunyīre ria itina-inī cia mītī īrīa mīnini.
english: Do hand weeding around the young trees.

kikuyu: Huthīra icembe rīrīa ūkūrima gatagatī ka mīkaro.
english: Use implements like the half-moon jembe to weed in between the rows.

kikuyu: kūngīkinyīrīra atī kwīna ria rīrīa rītahukaga raithi ta thangari, hubīra mītī na bucket kana iratathi mbere ya kūhūra dawa ya ria.
english: In the event that there are stubborn weeds like couch grass, cover the seedlings (with a bucket or bag) before spraying the weeds with a suitable herbicide.

kikuyu: Nī mīmera īrīkū īngīhandanīrio na kahūa?
english: Which crops can you intercrop with coffee?

kikuyu: mīmera īrīa mīega ya kuhandanīria na kahūa nī īrīa yoyaga kahinda kanini gūkūra ta mboco, nyanya na waru cia ngwacī .
english: Suitable intercrops include short leguminous crops such as beans, tomatoes and Irish potatoes.

kikuyu: Handa mīmera īno ya gatagatī ūkīhūthīra bataraitha īrīa njītīkīrie ta NPK-17:17:17.
english: Plant the intercrops using a recommended fertilizer preferably NPK fertilizer such as 17:17:17.

kikuyu: Handa mīmera ino gatagatī-inī ka raini cia kahūa ūtigītie ta fiti 2 kuuma gītina-inī gia kahūa.
english: Plant the intercrop at the middle of the inter rows at least 2 feet away from the coffee rows/stem.

kikuyu: Kahūa kangīhandanīrio na mīmera īrīkū īngī?
english: What to intercrop coffee with?

kikuyu: Mīmera mīega na īrī umithio ībatiī kūhandanīrio na kahūa nī waru, nyanya hamwe na mboco.
english: The technically and economically viable intercrops for coffee were potatoes, tomatoes, beans, and tomatoes in combination with beans.

kikuyu: Kahūa kamenyagīrīrwo atīa?
english: How to maintain a coffee plantation?

kikuyu: Cokereria mīūngūrwa īrīa ītanagwata, thondeka mūceng'i na urīmīre, ceha kahūa ūrīa kwagīrīire na gūkahe bataraitha, kagitīre kuumana na tūtambi na mīrimū.
english: replace seedlings that have not grown, keep the soil covered and remove weeds, prune the coffee trees correctly, apply fertilizers, protect the coffee trees from insects and diseases.

kikuyu: Mbegū cia kahūa ingīongererwo ūritū atīa?
english: How to increase coffee berry weight?

kikuyu: Nitrogen – Nitrogen nīyabata mūmera ūgīkūra, no īngīkīra kihūa gīgīkūrū, ūnene wa mbegū nīūhatīkagwo.
english: Nitrogen Nitrogen is needed for good growth, but too much at later stages of crop maturity can compromise coffee berry size.

kikuyu: Potassium – Potasium nīyendagwo kwa wūīngī kahūa gagīkīra mbegū na gūteithia igīe sukari wakūigana.
english: Potassium High supplies of potassium are needed during berry set and berry fill to maximize sugar accumulation in berry and eventual bean.

kikuyu: Potassium īteithagia kūnenehia mbegū na kūmīhe mūcamo na njīra ya gūcitwarīra cukari kuuma mathangū-inī.
english: Potassium has a crucial role to play in improving coffee berry size and quality through its role in the movement of sugars from the leaf for accumulation in the fruit.

kikuyu: īkoragwo igīthiūrūrūka mūmera-inī na makīria rīrīa mbegū irekīra, nīūndū ūyū, mūthithū ūrīa ūrī mathangū-inī no ūthire na kīhua kīambīrīrie kūūma.
english: It is mobile in the tree and during peak periods of growth – particularly fruit fill – reserves in the leaves can soon become depleted, leading to dieback.

kikuyu: Boron – Boron ya mathangū nīyabata mūno harī kūnenehia mbegū na kūhe kahūa gredi njega.
english: Boron Foliar boron has a significant positive effect on coffee berry size – improving the quality grade of coffee beans.

kikuyu: ona ningī kūhūra boron o ihinda rīrīa rīagīrīire gūtūmaga mūmera ūgīe na mathangū wega ūū atī mbegū nayo igakorwo īrī na mūcamo mwega.
english: However, foliar sprays can provide a good, in-season top-up response, raising leaf levels such that coffee production and bean quality are maintained.

kikuyu: Mīūngūrwa igaitīīrīrio maaī kaingī nginya īgīe hinya wa kūhandwo harīa mītī īgūkūrīra.
english: The seedlings will be watered frequently and shaded from bright sunlight until they are hearty enough to be permanently planted.

kikuyu: Kahūa kangīambīrīria gūtukanio na mīmera īngī mīaka īrī thutha wa kūhandwo.
english: Intercropping can be undertaken within the first two years after establishment.

kikuyu: īkīra grams mīrongo ītano cia CAN mīeri 6 thutha wa kūhanda.
english: Apply 50g of CAN per seedling six months after planting.

kikuyu: Thutha wa mwaka umwe, īkīra grams mīrongo īnana cia NPK ta 17:17:17 o harī gītina gīa kahūa.
english: After one year, apply 80g of NPK e.g. 17:17:17 per tree.

kikuyu: Mīaka īrī na nuthu yathira, īkīra grams igana rīmwe cia CAN. Ningī thutha wa mīaka īrī, īkīra grams 125 cia NPK harī o mūtī.
english: One and half year apply 100g of CAN. At two years, apply NPK at 125g per tree.

kikuyu: Mekīra macio mangīmarūmīrīre mataaro. Mīaka īrī ya mbere, reke mahūa magwe nīguo mītī īmere honge nyingī.
english: Subsequent applications should be as per the recommendations. For the first two years, abort the flowers to encourage vegetative growth.

kikuyu: Boron īteithagīrīria thuna kuumīra na gūteithīrīria kūruta mahūa na gwikīra mbegū .
english: Boron – promotes shoot growth and facilitates optimal flowering/fruit set.

kikuyu: Zinc īteithagia ihūa gūthondekwo na gūkūra wega. Ningī nīgiragīrīria kīhūa gwītiria heho.
english: Zinc – promotes flower bud formation and development. It also increases the coffee plant resistance to cold.

kikuyu: Calcium iteithagia mīthondekere ya ihūa rīa kahūa.
english: Calcium – enhances formation and growth of terminal buds/flower.

kikuyu: Mabataraitha marīa mega ma mathangū marīa mateithagia kīhūa kūruta mahūa nī hamwe na Omex Zibo( omexoliar boron) ya Omex, Oshbor ya Osho chemicals na Agrigrow (Zinc + Boron) ya Agrichem Africa.
english: Some of the best foliar fertilizers for increased flowering and bud formation include: Omex Zibo (Omex Foliar Boron) by Omex Oshbor by Osho Chemicals, Agrigrow (Zinc + Boron) by Agrichem Africa

kikuyu: Nī ihinda rīrīkū rīega rīa gwīkīra bataraitha kahūa-inī?
english: When to fertilize coffee plant?

kikuyu: Mītī ya kahūa no īraihe fiti nyingīna igūrū, kwoguo gwīkīra bataraitha kaingīna kūmīthamia o ūria īrakura nogūteithie gūkūria kahūa kega!
english: Coffee Plants can grow several feet tall at their fullest height, so regular fertilizing and repotting can help your Coffee Plant manage healthy growth!

kikuyu: Hūthīra bataraitha īrīa yagīrīire o thutha wa mīeri 2 kana 3 ihinda rīa ūrugarī. Ndugekīre bataraitha hīndī ya heho nīūndū mūtī hīndī īyo ūkoragwo ūkīhurūka.
english: Fertilize with a balanced houseplant fertilizer every 2-3 months in warmer seasons. Don't fertilize in the fall and winter while the plant is resting

kikuyu: Mūtaratata ūrīa mwega wa kūhe kahūa bataraitha nī ūrīkū?
english: What is the fertilizer management for coffee?

kikuyu: Bataraitha yagīrīirwo gwīkīrwo kahūa-inī ta ūū -180g Nitrogen (N), -90g Phosphorus (P), - 180g Potassium (K).
english: Currently, the fertilizer recommended rate (RR) for coffee is 180 Nitrogen (N)- 90 Phosphorus (P)- 180 Potassium (K).

kikuyu: Icigo-inī iria irūmagīrīra mītaratara ya gūtūkania mīmera nī ta Cavite na icigo ingī, yagīrīirwo gwīkīrwo ūū o harī hectare:200-100- 200 na kuongererwo micronutrients iria irendeka kūringana na ithimi cia tīīri.
english: In areas following the multiple cropping system such as Cavite and other provinces, it is recommended to apply 200-100-200 per hectare plus the needed micronutrients depending on soil analysis

kikuyu: Nī bataraitha īrīkū yagīrīire rīrīa kahūa karuta kīro?
english: What is the best fertilizer for coffee flowering?

kikuyu: Magnesium na Sulphur nīiteithagia kuongerera maciro na kuoguo itibatie kwaga ihinda ona rīmwe.
english: Magnesium and sulfur have a positive effect on coffee yield and supplies should not be limiting throughout the season.

kikuyu: Zinc na Boron nīciabata mūno ihinda rīa kūruta kīro nīūndū nīītūmaga mbegū cīige wega na igatūma kahūa gaciare wega.
english: Zinc and Boron are particularly important at the flowering stage to improve berry set and overall coffee yield potential.

kikuyu: Mītī ya kahūa ībataraga Potash nyingī, Nitrogen nyingī na Phosphoric acid nini.
english: Coffee trees need a lot of potash, a lot of nitrogen, and a little phosphoric acid.

kikuyu: Thiūrūrūkīria bataraitha iyo o gītina-inī gīa kahūa ūmenyereire ndugaitīīrīrie mathangū kana gītina-inī gīa kahūa.
english: Spread the fertilizer in a ring around each coffee tree, but be very careful not to put any on its trunk, branches or leaves.

kikuyu: Urea nī bataraitha njega na kahūa?
english: Is urea fertilizer good for coffee?

kikuyu: Nitrogen nīyo nutrient īrīa mūmera wa kahūa ūhūthagīra mūno na nīyo nutrient ya keerī īheanagwo nī mbegū cia kahūa.
english: Nitrogen is the nutrient most extracted by the coffee plant and the nutrient of second greatest export by coffee beans

kikuyu: Bataraitha ya DAP nī njega harī kahūa ?
english: Is DAP fertilizer good for coffee?

kikuyu: Īno īkoragwo ītukanītie macro na micro nutrients iria ikinyanagīra thutha wa bataraitha ya mīrī na mathangū gūīkirwo.
english: This includes both macro and micronutrients which is achieved through application of both basal and foliar fertilizers

kikuyu: Nīguo maciaro maingī moneke, mūmera no mūhaka ūheyo irio cia kūigana
english: For an optimal production, the crop should be provided with a proper nutrition.

kikuyu: Nīgūkorwo urea īkoragwo na Nitrogen nyingī makīrīa, yagīrīire gūtukanio na tīīri kana mūthanga ītanekīrwo mūmera-inī.
english: Since Urea is highly Nitrogen-concentrated, it should be used in combination with earth or sand before its application.

kikuyu: Urea ndīagīrīire gwīkīrwo rīrīa tīīri wīna maaī maingī kana ugūikara ūrī mūigū ta thikū 3 kana 4 thutha wa gwīkīrwo.
english: Urea should not be applied when the soil contains free water or likely to remain wet for three or four days after application.

kikuyu: Nī rīera rīrīkū rīega rīa gūkūria kahūa Kenya?
english: What is the best climate for coffee farming in Kenya?

kikuyu: Kahūa kaingī gakūraga gatagatī-inī ka matūra marīa mita 1400 -2000 igūrū wa iria na tīīri-inī mūtune na mūriku wūikūrūkagia maaī wega.
english: Most coffee grows at altitudes between 1400 and 2000 metres in deep, well-drained volcanic soils.

kikuyu: Ūrugarī wa gatagatī-inī ka digirii 15 na 24 na mbura ītarī nene mūno ya gatagatī-inī ka ithimo cia milimita 900 nginya 1200.
english: Temperatures range from 15 to 24 degrees and average rainfall ranges from 900–1200mm.

kikuyu: Matīna ma gūkūra kwa mbegū nī marīkū?
english: What are the stages of coffee fruiting?

kikuyu: ITĪNA RĪA MBERE Wiki īmwe nginya mūgwanja(thikū 0 nginya 50) thutha wa ihūa gūcanūka. Mbegū īgakūra kahora na īgakorwo īigana ta kīongo gīa kībiriti
english: STAGE 1. 1-7 weeks (0 -50 days) after blooming. Slow Growth stage; the fruit is as big as the tip of a match.

kikuyu: ITĪNA RĪA KEERĪ Wiki ya kanana nginya ikūmi na mūgwanja (thikū 50 -120) kuuma Ihūa rīacanūka.Mbegū īgakūra na ihenya, na īkagīa na gelatine .
english: STAGE 2. 8-17 weeks (50-120 days) after blooming. The fruit grows quickly; the seed has a gelatinous consistency.

kikuyu: ITĪNA RĪA GATATŪ Wiki ya ikūmi na kanana nginya ya mīrongo īrī na ītano (thikū 120-180) kuuma ihūa rīacanūka. Mbegū īkarīkia gūkūra, īkaiyūria na īkagīa na ūritū.
english: STAGE 3 18–25 weeks (120–180 days) after blooming. The seed completes its development, acquires a solid consistency and gains weight.

kikuyu: ITĪNA RĪA KANA Wiki ya mīrongo īrī na ītandatū nginya mīrongo ītatū na ithathatū (thikū 180 – 224 kuuma ihūa gūcanūka. Mbegū ikambīrīria gūtuta. Thutha wa wiki 32, makīria ma thikū 224, mbegū cieruha makīria ikagarūrūka rangi igatuīka cia purple njirīrīru, na ikoma.
english: STAGE 4 26–32 weeks (180–224 days) after blooming. Fruit is physiologically developed and begins to mature. After week 32 (more than 224 days), fruit over-ripens and turns dark purple. Finally, it dries.
