kikuyu: Nī njīra īrīkū njega ya kūringithania thogora wa irio itiganīte īngīhee ng'ombe ciakwa?
english: How do I calculate the cost-effectiveness of different feed options for my dairy cows?

kikuyu: Ngarama ya irio na thogora wa iria nīcio ituaga baida ya ūrithi.
english: feed costs and farm gate price of milk determine the profitability of a dairy enterprise.

kikuyu: Ūndū ūyū wītagwo mūigana ūria mūnene wa magetha.
english: This is termed maximum production.

kikuyu: Thogora wa iria ūngīkorwo wīmūnene, nogūo baida īnenehaga.
english: If the milk price is high, this method may coincide with maximum profit.

kikuyu: Ūndū ūyū wonekaga rīrīa irio cia mūtu irī nagoro mūno.
english: This happens when the cost of concentrate is too high.

kikuyu: Thogora wa iria ningī nīūringanaga na kūria mūgūnda ūri, kana itūra.
english: Farm gate price of milk also depends on location, with peri-urban farmers getting better prices.

kikuyu: Mīgūnda iria īkūhīrīirie mataūni nīyendagia iria na thogora mwegega. Mūtaratara mwega wa gūthondeka baida njega wonekaga rīria ngarama yakūrīithia ī nini, na thogora wa iria nī ūīkaine.
english: A true maximum profit ration program includes a least-cost function, incorporates milk price information, and uses maximum profit (income over feed cost) as one of the constraints or specifications on which to formulate.

kikuyu: Nī irio cia mūthemba ūrīkū ciagīrīire kūheo ng'ombe cia iria hindī ya gūciciarithania?
english: What are the nutritional needs of dairy cows during the breeding season?

kikuyu: Mori no cirīithīrio ciieni-inīnjega nīgukorwo ūbatari wa irio kana nutrients ti mūnene (gūkūra na kūgacīrithia).
english: Heifers can be reared on good-quality pasture as their nutrient requirements are low (growth and maintenance).

kikuyu: Irio cia mūtu ciagīrīire kūongererwo na gīthimi kīa 1% kīa ūritū wa mori na 12-14% proteini iria cīigīirwo mahuti mūthemba wa legumes na 15-16% angīkorwo nī nyeki.
english: Supplementation with concentrate should be at 1% of body weight with 12–14% crude protein for heifers on legume forage and 15–16% crude protein on grass forage.

kikuyu: Protein nī yabata mūno kūrī mori irakūra nīguo kūgacīrithia ūnene, ūraihu ona kūongerera ūritū.
english: Protein is extremely important in the diet of growing heifers to ensure adequate frame size, wither height and growth.

kikuyu: Wītheme mori nguhī na njīra ya gūcihe irio njega īrī na protein ya kūigana.
english: Avoid short heifers by balancing the ration and including enough crude protein.

kikuyu: Mori īngīheo irio nyingī cia hinya, mūkamo ndūkuraga wega niūndū wa maguta kūingīra nyondo-inī na no yage kūruta iria wega ihinda rīakinya rīa gūkamwo.
english: Feeding heifers too much energy leads to fat infiltrating the mammary glands, inhibiting development of secretory tissue, thus reducing milk yield.

kikuyu: Ningī kūhe irio nini gūcungagīrīria mori ikagīa mīrī mīnini, ūndū ūyū ūkarehe ūgwati hindī ya gūciara yakinya.
english: Underfeeding results in small-bodied heifers, which experience difficulty during calving (dystocia).

kikuyu: Kūhe mori irio nyingī cia hinya na protein nini gūtūmaga ikūre irī noru na igakuhīha, ningī ungīcihe irio cia hinya itarī njiganu īgatūma mori ikūre irī njeke na ndaihū.
english: Overfeeding heifers on feed high in energy but low in protein results in short, fat heifers; high protein and low energy feed results in tall, thin heifers

kikuyu: Thīna ūyū ūrūagwo naguo na njīra ya kūhe maaī maingī. Ningī nowikīre huhirio kana wikīre feni cia kūhurutīra thīinī wa ciūngū cia ng'ombe.
english: By providing enough water. You may also ensure ventilation within the dairy unit by providing enough ventilations or introducing fans

kikuyu: Carbohydrates, amino acids, fatty acids, cumbī, vitamins na maaī ciothe nī ciabata mahinda mothe.
english: Carbohydrates, amino acids, fatty acids, minerals, vitamins, and water are all important at this stage.

kikuyu: Ūrīithi mwega wa mahiū wambagīrīria rīrīa ng'ombe cia gūciarithania iracagūrwo na kūrūmīrīra mītugo mīega ya ūrīithi.
english: Good animal husbandry starts at breed selection and good animal husbandry practices.

kikuyu: Ingīhota atia kūgacīrithia mīrīre ya ng'ombe iria ihingagīrwo?
english: How do I manage nutrition for dairy cows in intensive housing systems?

kikuyu: Ūgūcihe irio kūringana na bata wa ngurubu īyo.
english: Ensuring that you group your cows into age groups so that you provide feeds depending on the needs of each cow.

kikuyu: Ingīgacīrithia atia mīhere na kūnyihia wanangi wa irio ūrīithi-inī wa ng'ombe ya iria?
english: How do I optimize feed efficiency and reduce feed waste in dairy cow nutrition programs?

kikuyu: Hebata gūthūrima mūigana wa nutrients irio-inī nīguo gutigīrīra irio icio nī nginyaniru.
english: Regularly evaluate the nutrient composition of feed ingredients to ensure accurate ration formulation.

kikuyu: Nīwega gūthima irio cia ng'ombe nīguo kūmenya kana nīirī na ūkinyanīru wa nutrients ūrīa wagīrīire.
english: Conduct feed tests to determine the quality and nutritional value of the feed.

kikuyu: Mahuti ta silage o na marīa momithie ta nyeki, nī mabata ūrīithi-inī.
english: Optimize Forage Quality: Forages, such as hay and silage, are crucial components of a dairy cow's diet.

kikuyu: Ūhoro ūyū ūteithagia kūmenya ūtiganu maūndū morū marīa mangįkorwo makīyumīria kana ona ūtiganu ūria ūngikorwo wīho na kūhotithia kwoya ikinya rīrīa riagīrīire.
english: This information helps identify any variations or potential issues and allows adjustments to be made to the ration if needed.

kikuyu: Gūtukania matigari na mīthemba īngī ya magetha no ūkorwo ūrī mūbango ūtarī na goro.
english: Incorporating by-products and alternative feeds can be a cost-effective strategy.

kikuyu: Kwa mūhiano, matigari ma īganda cia njohi, mīgate o na macica nī imwe cia ihumo cia irio cia ng'ombe.
english: For example, distillers’ grains, bakery waste, or citrus pulp can be used as alternative feed sources.

kikuyu: Nī mīrimū īrikū īgūmagīra ng'ombe cia iria mūno gūkū Kenya?
english: What are the common diseases affecting dairy cows in Kenya?

kikuyu: Mīrīmū ino nī hamwe na mastitis, mūūrirū, foot and mouth na milk fever.
english: mastitis,anthrax,Black Quarter,Foot-and-mouth cattle disease,Milk fever cattle disease

kikuyu: Ingīhota atia kūgitīra na kūrūa na mūrimū wa mūkamo rūūru-inī rwa ng'ombe cia iria?
english: How do I prevent and control mastitis in my dairy herd?

kikuyu: Mūrimū ūyū wambagia kuoneka rīrīa njamuthi ici ciingīra nyondo-inī na gūciaranīra kūu thīinī.
english: Infections begin when microorganisms penetrate the teat canal and multiply in the mammary gland.

kikuyu: Ndariri nī hamwe na kūimba, ruo na gūtunīha kwa mūkamo
english: Symptoms include swelling, pain, and redness of the udder.

kikuyu: Ingīhota atīa gūthondeka mūtaratara ngūrūmīrīra wa kūrigīrīria mūrimū wa mūkam mūgūnda-inī wakwa?
english: How do I implement a mastitis prevention program on my farm?

kikuyu: Nīwega gūkamīra ng'ombe thīinī wa mūthaigū nīguo kūrigīrīria nyondo kūgīa na nguraro o na gūtambia njamuthi kuuma kūrī ng’ombe imwe nginya īrīa īngī.
english: By using proper milking technique in the parlor to prevent teat injury and cow-to-cow transmission of pathogens.

kikuyu: Ningī nī wega kūrūmīrīra mītaratara ya ūhūthīri wa dawa īrīa yagīrīire kūringana na mataaro ma mūthondeki.
english: Antibiotic dry cow therapy used according to label specifications

kikuyu: Njanjo cia mūrimū wa ngaaī nīigitagīra ng’ombe cia iria na hihi ng'ombe ībatiī gūthecwo maita maigana?
english: Is east coast fever vaccinations necessary to protect dairy cows and how often should they be administered?

kikuyu: Njanjo ya mūrimū wa ngaaī īrīa ītagwo ECF Muguga Vaccine, nīya gīkīro kīa igūru na nī īhūthīkīte na īkonania mawega mabūrūri marīa marī rūgūrū, gatagatī na mūhuro wa Africa (Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Malawi, Zambia na Zimbambwe) harī kūhūrana na mūrimū wa ngaaī.
english: ECF Muguga Vaccine is a quality vaccine and is used successfully across East, Central and Southern Africa (Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe) against east coast fever.

kikuyu: Hebata wa kūhūra ng'ombe dawa ya kūūraga ngūha tondū nīitambagia mūrimū wa ngaaī na mīrimū īngī. Ng'ombe ibatiī kūigwo na ūgima mwega wa mwīrī hīngo ciothe.
english: It is still necessary to spray against ticks as ticks carry other disease besides mild exposure to ticks is important to keep your animals immune for life.

kikuyu: ūria ndagītarī wa mahiū maakū rīrīa ūbatiī kūhuhīrīria dawa ya ngūha.
english: Ask your vet for advice on how often to spray against ticks.

kikuyu: Njanjo ya ngaaī no īheo njaū ya ūkūrū wa mūeri ūmwe.
english: Can be used in calves from one month of age.

kikuyu: Njanjo īmwe tu īgitagīra ng'ombe kuumana na mūrimū wa ngaaī mūtūrīre wayo woothe.
english: One vaccination shot protects your animal against ECF for life.

kikuyu: Ingīhota atīa kūrigīrīria na kūrūa na ngūha rūūru-inī rwakwa ?
english: How do I prevent and control tick infestations in my dairy herd?

kikuyu: Arīithi a mahiū mahūthagīra dawa cia mūnanda kūūraga ngūha.
english: Livestock owners reduce the effects of ticks mainly through tick control using chemicals known as acaricides.

kikuyu: Mīhīrīga nī mīingī ya dawa cia mūnanda kūringana na indo iria icithodekete na mūrutire wacio wa wīra.
english: Acaricides come from different groups identified by their active ingredients, with different modes of action to kill the ticks.

kikuyu: Nī njīra irīkū njega cia kūrūa na mīnyoo kana njoka ng’ombe-inī cia iria?
english: What are the best practices for deworming dairy cows?

kikuyu: Nīguo kūrūa na mīnyoo, rūūru rwothe rūheo dawa.
english: To control worms, deworm your herd.

kikuyu: Nī kwendekithītio atī dawa ya njoka īheo na njīra ya gūkundio nīguo imerie yothe.
english: It is recommended to do drenching when deworming to ensure the cow swallow the dose of the drug.

kikuyu: Njaū nī ibataīre kūheo dawa cia mīnyoo īrī na mīeri īna na ikarūmīrīra kūheo o thutha wa mīeri ītandatū.
english: Dose calves with recommended anthelmintics at 4 months and every 6 months thereafter.

kikuyu: Hihi njanjo cia mūrimū wa mūūrirū nī cia bata harī kūgitīra ng'ombe na ibatiī kūheo maita maigana?
english: Is anthrax vaccinations necessary to protect dairy cows and how often should they be administered?

kikuyu: Mūrimū wa mūūrirū būrūri-inī wa Kenya nīguo ūtongoretie harī mīrimū īria īgwatanagio kuuma kūrī nyamū gūthiī kūrī andū. Ūū nī kūringana na ūthuthuria ūrīa wonanītie atī mūrimū ūyū nīūgūmagīra andū na biacara ciao na nīngī no ūthereme kūnene gwa kahinda kanini.
english: In Kenya, Anthrax is the highest ranked zoonotic disease, based on a systematic analysis of burden, socio economic impact, epidemic potential, and severity of zoonotic diseases.

kikuyu: Riboti ya national public health and veterinary yonanītie atī mītuthūko o ikūmi ya mūrimū wa mūūrirū nīīgwatagio andū o mwaka.
english: According to national public health and veterinary records, an average of 10 Anthrax outbreaks involving animals with spill- over to humans occur every year.

kikuyu: Nīkwedekithītio atī njanjo irūmanīrīrio mīaka ītatū thutha wa mūtuthūko itūrū-inī rīna nīguo kūnina mūrimū wa mūūrirū kaimana. Nīwega hīndī ciothe kwaranīria na ndagītarī wa mahiū nīguo agūtare.
english: Annual vaccination for three consecutive years after an outbreak to break the infection cycle in an area is recommended. Always consult your local vet for recommendations.

kikuyu: Hihi nī njīra īrīkū ingīhota kūrigīrīria ndangūrū na mīnyoo ng'ombe-ini cia iria?
english: How do I manage and prevent internal worms in dairy cattle?

kikuyu: Aranīria na ndagitarī wa mahiū ūgīthondeka mītaratara ya kūhe ng'ombe dawa cia mīnyoo.
english: Always consult your vet to assist in coming up with a deworming program together and recommendations.

kikuyu: Hihi ndariri cia mathīna ma ūciari ng'ombe-inī cia iria nī irīkū na ingīrigīrīria mathīna maya atīa?
english: What are the signs of reproductive disorders in dairy cows, and how do I address them?

kikuyu: Ūhoti wa ūciari ūcangagīrwo nī maūndū marīa matūrigicīirie,mītungatīre na maūthī ma ūciarī.
english: The efficiency of reproduction is influenced by the interactive effect of environment, management, and genetic factors.

kikuyu: Ningī mīrimū ya ng'ombe cia iria nī inyihagia maciaro kaingī na njīra ya kūnyihia matukū marīa ng'ombe īikaraga īngīciaraga na īkanyia iria.
english: Furthermore, diseases commonly affect dairy cow productivity by decreasing reproductive efficiency, shortening the expected length of productive life, and lowering milk production.

kikuyu: Mīrimū ya ūciari nī hamwe na kwaga kūonania mūrukī, RB, kūremwo nīkūruta thigira hamwe na kūhuna kūria gūcangagīra makīrīa ma gīcunjīkīa mīrongo īnana harī igana kūrī nyamū ciothe dwaru.
english: The major reproductive problems are anestrus, RB, retention of fetal membrane, and abortions which contributed >80% of the total affected animals.

kikuyu: Hihi ingeka atīa gūkinyanīria ūtheru njoku-inī nīguo iria rīkorwo rīrīi theru?
english: How do I ensure proper hygiene and sanitation in the milking parlor to prevent milk contamination?

kikuyu: Mītugo mīega nī hamwe na gūtheria njoku, gūthambia moko na nyondo hamwe na indo ciothe cia gūkamīra na kūiga iria, gūthecithia njanjo na kūrigita, na gūte iria rīothe rīa ng'ombe ndwaru kana iria iraheo dawa cia kūrigita.
english: Practices included milking parlour cleanliness, hand and udder cleaning, milking and storage containers, cleaning of milk containers, cow's vaccination and treatment and discarding milk from sick or treated cows

kikuyu: Ng'ombe ihingagirwo na kuogwo ikahūthīra hinya mūingī wa kuuma irio-inī gūkūra na gūthondeka iria.
english: Cows are confined and therefore use most of the energy from feeds for growth and milk production.

kikuyu: Nīkūhotekithagia ūtheru wa iria.
english: • Clean milk production is possible.

kikuyu: Nīkūhotekithagia mūrerere mwega wa njaū.
english: • Good calf rearing is possible

kikuyu: Thumu ni ūcokanagīrīrio kwa njīra hūthū na gūtwarwo mūgūnda wa mahuti.
english: • Manure can be easily collected for the benefit of fodder crops

kikuyu: Ng'ombe nīigitagīrwo kuuma na mīrimū, makīria īrīa īrehagwo nī ngūha.
english: • The animals are better protected against diseases, especially tick-borne diseases.

kikuyu: Kūrora ng'ombe wega na kūmenya rīrīa irī mūrukīū o na gūcitungata nī kūhūthaga.
english: • Close observation of the animals is possible, making heat detection and attendance to animals easier and faster.

kikuyu: Ng'ombe hingīre nīngitīre kuuma kūrī thū. Ningī nī kūhonokagia ihinda rīa kūrīithia, ūguo ihinda rīu rīkahūthīka kūruta wīra ūngī.
english: • The animals are kept inside which is more secure and protect them from attack by predators • Little or no time is spent on herding the animals. Therefore labour for other farm tasks is saved

kikuyu: Nī maūndū marīkū moru mangīkorūo moimanīte na ūrīithi wa kūhingīra ng'ombe?
english: What are the disadvantages of zero grazing?

kikuyu: Nī wīra mūnene wa kūhe ng'ombe irio na maaī.
english: Much labour is required to take feed and water to the animals.

kikuyu: Ningī mbeca nyingī nīibataranagia rīrīa kiūgū gīgwakwo.
english: • Much capital is required for construction of a ‘zero-grazing unit.

kikuyu: Nī kūrī ūgwati wa ng'ombe gūtangīka nīūndū wa kūhingīrwo ihinda iraya.
english: • The possibility that animals are stressed because of too much confinement inside the zero grazing unit

kikuyu: Nī maūndū marīkū ma bata maroragwo waki-inī wa ciugū cia ng’ombe?
english: What are the key considerations for construction of a zero grazing unit?

kikuyu: Tigīrira fundi niaranyabarwo nī abithaa wa mahiū rīrīa araka nīguo kūrigīrīria mahītia kūhanīka waki-inī.
english: Ensure that the fundi (constructor) is supervised by a Livestock Extension Officer during the construction of the unit.

kikuyu: Ūyū nīūndū wabata nīūndū mwako ūmwe ta waharīa ng'ombe īkinyaga īkīria harīkia gwako nī hagūtūra.
english: This is necessary because some parts (ie walking area, troughs) once constructed are permanent.

kikuyu: Mahītia ma mīako nomakorwo goro kūrūnga.
english: Mistakes made during construction can be very costly.

kikuyu: ii. Tigīrira gwakwo mūgūnda-inīharīa hagarīire, kūringana na kūrīa rūhuho rūhurutanaga.
english: ii. Ensure that the correct site, considering the direction of wind, is chosen for the unit.

kikuyu: Gūthuurwo kwa handū harīa mahiū megwakīrwo nīgūteithagia harī kūgitīra mahiū mau kuumana na mbura, riūa, na maūndū mangī ma rīera.
english: The choice of site influences the security and protection of animals from rain, sunshine and other weather effects.

kikuyu: Nīwega kūmenya atī kūgitīra ng'ombe kuuma kūrī mbura nī gwabata makīria kūrī kuuma kūrī riūa kana rūhuho.
english: It should be noted that it is more important to protect an animal from the rain than from wind or sunshine.

kikuyu: v. Mūthia, nīwega kwirūmbūiya na gūthodekaga ciūgu haria ciathūka. Ūyū kaingī nīūndū wabata mūno makīria nīūndū wa harīa ng’ombe ithiagīra kana īrūgamaga īkīria.
english: v. Finally, one should as much as possible, carry out regular maintenance of the zero-grazing unit while in use. This is usually very important for the walking area.

kikuyu: Ng'ombe irabatara kūheyo maaī kwa wūingī, gwakīrwo kiugū kīna rūgito na kīretekīria rīera gūcera wega.
english: By providing dairy cows with plenty of drinking water all the time, providing shade and ventilation.

kikuyu: Arīmi amwe nīmarī ūhoti wa kūgūra ibīrīrīki cia kūhūra ūrugarī ciūgu-inī cia ng'ombe.
english: Some farmers with resources can use fans to help cows dissipate heat.

kikuyu: Ng’ombe nīiheraga rīrīa irī kūndū kūrī na riūa ihiū ona kūrī na ciīruru cia mītī.
english: In warm areas with bright sunlight and when there are no shade trees, the temperatures within the shed can be too high to be comfortable for dairy cattle.

kikuyu: Ūndū ūyū no ūgirīrīke na njīra ya kwongerera mūgeka kana nyeki rūngū rwa mambarita kana gūthondeka njīra ya kūruta rīera rīrīa ihiū. Njīra īno noithondekwo na gwaka ngito igīrī, īmwe igūrū wa īria īngī.
english: This effect can be overcome by having an overlay of cadjan or straw or by having a warm air outlet on the roof. The warm air outlet can be provided by having the roof at two levels

kikuyu: Floo ībatiī gūkorwo īrī niaru wega, īhe ng'ombe ūrume wa gūkinyukīa na īkorwo ya gūtūra.
english: provides a relatively dry walking surface,provides confident and comfortable footing, and provides confidence and is durable.

kikuyu: Hihi bataire gūtigīrīra atīa gīko gīothe nīkīrauma ciūgū-inī cia ng'ombe na gūkīiga na njīra njega nīguo nyihie ūgwati ūngīhotomia ūgima wa mwīrī wa ng'ombe?
english: How do I ensure proper drainage and waste management in dairy cattle housing to prevent health issues?

kikuyu: Thondeka mītaro mīega ya gūite gīko na maaī kūraihu na kiugū
english: construct cross-drains to carry run-off into existing drains on the edge of the dairy unit.

kikuyu: Tigīrīra atī gīko nīgīatherera kūndū gūtarī ithima cia maaī kana bara-inī.
english: Ensure this is diverted off the track and not onto other low areas in the track or into watercourses.

kikuyu: Hihi nī ithimo irīkū ciagīrīire harī gwakīra ng'ombe imwe ya iria kana nyingī?
english: What are the recommended dimensions for individual and group housing for dairy cows?

kikuyu: Kiugū gīothe gībataiī kūrigicīrio ni rūthingo rwa ūraihu wa futi 5 mīena ītatū na mwena ūmwe ūkorwo na mūharatī.
english: The entire shed should be surrounded by a boundary wall of. 5" height from three side and manger etc., on one side.

kikuyu: Handū ha kūrīira habatie gūkorwo na futi 2 nginya 2.5 harī o ng'ombe.
english: The feeding area should be provided with 2 to 2 ½ feet of manger space per cow.

kikuyu: Mūharati wa maai ūkorwo na ūraihu wa futi 10 nigūo wīkīragwo maaī matheru ma kūnyua.
english: All along the manger, there shall be 10" wide water trough to provide clean, even, available drinking water

kikuyu: Hihi ingīka atīa nīgwo kiugū gīkorwo na ūtheri mūiganu nīgetha ng'ombe īikare wega na īhote kuongerera iria?
english: How do I provide adequate lighting in dairy cattle housing to promote cow comfort and productivity?

kikuyu: Maya no macenjio na mahinda kūringana na rīera.
english: This can be regulated over time as the climatic conditions change

kikuyu: Kiugū gīake wega na kīrore wega nī gītūmaga ng'ombe itige kūrūgama mūno, ningī ikahota gūcokia makambī, ūtheru ūkahūtha na mītino īkanyiha.
english: Well designed and managed dairy cow freestalls (cubicles) can reduce excessive standing, allow more efficient rumination, improve cleanliness, and minimize injury.

kikuyu: Kūgayania kiugū nī gwabata waki-inī wa nyūmba cia mūthemba ūyū nīūndū ng'ombe nīīgīyaga handū hega ha gūkoma na kūhurūka.
english: Freestalls are a key component of a dairy freestall housing system and can provide a comfortable place for dairy cows to lie down and rest

kikuyu: Ingīka atīa nīguo gūkorwo na rīera rīega kiugū-inī kīa ng'ombe, nīguo kūhotithia ng'ombe kwaga kūhūthīra hinya mūingī wa kūrūa na ūrugarī ūngīkīra?
english: How do I ensure proper insulation in dairy cattle housing to regulate temperature and reduce energy costs?

kikuyu: Ūndū ūyū ūngīkinyanīra kūhetūkīra njira ngūrani ta kūhūthīra ibīririki, misters, spriklers ona kūhehia kūria ng'ombe ikomaga, marī maūndū ma kūnyihia ūrūgarī ūrīa ūhotomagia ūgima mwega wa mwīrī wa ng'ombe, kwūongerera iria na ūchiari.
english: This can be achieved by using various ways including fans, misters, sprinklers, and cooled waterbeds, to reduce the effect of thermal stress on cow health, production, and reproduction.

kikuyu: Nyūmba ici ibatiī gwakwo ūndū iretīkeria rīera gūcera wega.
english: The houses should also be constructed to allow free flow of air.

kikuyu: Hihi nī maūndū marīkū maroraguo rīrīa ūgwakīra harīa ng'ombe īgūciarīra?
english: What are the considerations for maternity or calving pens in dairy cattle housing?

kikuyu: Mataneti, kana harīa ng'ombe igūciarīra, habatiī gūkorwo hahūrītwo dawa ya kūūraga njamuthi, hakarwo iji ithathatu cia mahuti na riera rīgakorwo nīrīracera wega.
english: The maternity area should be disinfected, well bedded (6 inches), and well-ventilated.

kikuyu: Nyumba īno ībatiī gūkorwo īrī ya futi 100-150 harī o ng'ombe, nayo floo īkorwo īitītwo mūthanga, tīiri ūtarī mūnyitu kana wa rīumba nīguo kūhotithia ūtherū na ng'ombe kūrūgama wega.
english: The pen should provide 100-150 ft2 for each cow with flooring preferably of sand, dirt, or clay to aid in clean up and footing of the cow

kikuyu: Ingīka atīa nīguo hote gwakīra ng'ombe kiugū kiega mūgūnda-inī mūnini itekūwananga?
english: How do I optimize space utilization and layout efficiency in dairy cattle housing?

kikuyu: Cūbicles nī iteithagia kūhūthīra handū hanini na njīra njega.
english: Placing cubicles in buildings is an efficient use of space and bedding.

kikuyu: Ūndū ūyū nīūteithagia kūbanga mūcerere wa ng'ombe thīinī wa kiungū.
english: This controls movement of cows within the sheds/cubicles

kikuyu: Hihi njīra cia kūhingia mabataro ma maaī na irio ciugū-inī cia ng'ombe nī irīkū?
english: What are the options for feed and water management systems in dairy cattle housing?

kikuyu: Mūharatī wa kūrīra ūbatiī gūkorwo na ithimo cia futi 2 nginya 2.5 o harī ng'ombe.
english: The feeding area should be provided with 2 to 2 ½ feet of feeding trough space per cow.

kikuyu: Ningī nīgūbatiī gūkorwo na mūharatī ūrī na wariī wa futi ikūmi ūrīa ūrikīragwo maaī matheru hīndī ciothe.
english: All along the manger, there shall be 10" wide water trough to provide clean available drinking water.

kikuyu: Mūharatī ūyū wa maaī nīūnyihagia wanangī wa mahuti hīndī ya kūrīa.
english: The water trough thus constructed will also minimize the loss of fodders during feeding.

kikuyu: Hihi nīmoimerīra marīkū marehagwo nītūtambi twa kūruma ng'ombe cia iria na tūngītuhaana ta tūo?
english: What are the effects of biting insects and related pests on dairy cows?

kikuyu: Rūta matandīko ma ng'ombe na indo iria irahūthīka mbere ya gūthambia wega.
english: Remove all bedding and equipment before soaking and cleaning.

kikuyu: Ūrīa indo ici ithodeketwo naigūrū nīguo gūkūhotithia dawa ya kūūraga tūtambi kūruta wira wega.
english: The nature of the surfaces will influence the efficacy of the disinfection.

kikuyu: Angīkorwo naigūrū ti kūigananu, na kwīnamarima nogūo itangīhūrīka na dawa wega. Marima nīmagiragia indo kūhurīka wega.
english: Rough, porous surfaces are harder to disinfect than smooth surfaces. Porous surfaces are also harder to clean than smooth surfaces.

kikuyu: Dawa mūthemba wa hydrogen peroxide no ihūthīke.
english: A disinfectant based on hydrogen peroxide can be used

kikuyu: Hihi īngīgiria atīa nyūmba ya ng'ombe gūthūkio nī nyamū ta mbīya kana tūtambi?
english: How do I protect dairy cattle housing from pests, such as rodents or insects?

kikuyu: Tūtambi ta ngii, ndaa na mites cithīnagia ng'ombe cia iria mahinda matiganīte mwaka-inī.
english: Pests such as flies, lice, and mites usually occur on dairy animals at different times throughout the year.

kikuyu: Mīthemba mīingi ya ngii ta horn flies, stable flies o na horse/deer flies nīithīnagia ng'ombe.
english: Horn flies, stable flies, horse/deer flies, and others may be found on or around dairy animals.

kikuyu: Ngii ici inyuaga thakame na cionekaga mūno mwaka-inī rīrīa kūrī na ūrūgarī.
english: These flies are blood feeders and occur in the warmer times of the year.

kikuyu: Ndaa nacio kaingī cionekaga mūno mīeri-inī irīa mīhehū na o nacio inyuaga thakame.
english: Lice are generally found only in the cooler months of the year but are also blood feeders.

kikuyu: Ikamīro rībatiī gwakwo na indo cia mwanya nīguo kūhūthia gūthambia, kūnyihia ūgunyu, gūitīkīria rīera gūcera, gūbacīrīra ūrugarī, ūgitīīri kuumana na mwaki, kunyihia inegene na kūrehe ūtheri mūingī.
english: The various parts of the milking parlour require special construction materials and methods for ease of cleaning, moisture protection, ventilation, heating, fire protection, noise control, and illumination.

kikuyu: Maūndū maya mahutagia uciari wa ng'ombe; kūmenya rīrīa ng'ombe īkwenda ndume, ithaa rīrīa mūrūkī woneka na harīa ng'ombe īheyagīrwo mūbira, njīra īrīa mūbira ūharagīrio mbere ya gwīkirwo thīinī wa ng'ombe, warie wa njīra ya ūciari, na ng'ombe kūruta gīko gītheru īkīheo mbegu.
english: The following factors affect affect reproductive performance- estrous certainty, time of day of detected estrus and insemination, method of thawing semen, ease of cervix penetration, and presence of clear mucus at insemination.

kikuyu: Maūndū mangī mabata nī hamwe na maita marīa ng'ombe īheyagwo mbegu, mūthemba wa ndume, mūheani wa mbegū, ūkūrū wa ng'ombe irīa īraheo mūbira, ūrugarī wa ng'ombe īkīheo mbegū, na iria rīrīa īraruta.
english: Other important issues include service number, service sire, inseminator, age of cow, maximum ambient temperature on the service date, and milk yield.

kikuyu: Ūtungatī ta mīhere ya irio, nyūmba na mūthemba wa ng'ombe na marīa marigicīirie itūra ria kūria ng'ombe īrī, nī mahutagia uhoti wa gūciarana kwa ng'ombe.
english: The management practices like nutrition,housing and breed(genetic) of the cow and environmental factors also affect the reproduction.

kikuyu: Hihi ingīmenya atīa ihinda rīrīa riagīrīru ria kūhe ng'ombe mbegū nīguo hote kūgacīrithia guciarithania rūūru-inī rwaka?
english: How do I optimize estrus detection to maximize breeding success in my dairy herd?

kikuyu: Rīrīa ng'ombe īronania ndariri cia mūrūki, nīrio īkoragwo īkienda kūheo ndume na noīnyite ihu.
english: Estrus, commonly known as heat, is the period during which a cow is sexually receptive and can conceive.

kikuyu: Ihinda rīrī rīkoragwo ria mathaa 18-24 na rīcokagīra thutha wa thikū 21, o na gūkorwo no rīcenjie kuuma ng'ombe-inī īmwe nginya īrīa īngī.
english: This cycle typically lasts for 18-24 hours and occurs roughly every 21 days, although there can be variations among individual cows.

kikuyu: Kūmenya wega rīrīa ng'ombe īrenda ndume nīūndū wabata tondū nīgūteithagia mūrīmi kūheithia mbegū ihinda rīrīa riagīrīire na nīūndū ūcio, mīeke ya kūgwatia nīyongererekaga.
english: Detecting estrus accurately is vital because it enables farmers to inseminate the cow at the right time, maximizing the chances of conception.

kikuyu: Hihi ndariri cia ng'ombe irenda ndume nī irīkū na nīrī cionanagia mūrūkī?
english: What are the signs of heat (estrus) in dairy cows, and how often do they come into heat?

kikuyu: Ndariri cia mūrūkī nī hamwe na; ng'ombe kūgīa na wagagū na noikorwo ikienda gūcera mūno kūrī mūtūgo wacio.
english: Signs include :Increased Restlessness: Cows in estrus often exhibit restlessness and may walk or pace more than usual.

kikuyu: Kūruta mathambia njau; Kaingī gīko gīkiuma njīra ya ūciari nīkīonekaga, na gībatīī gūkorwo gītheru, gītenderū na kīragūcuka.
english: Mucus Discharge: There is often a noticeable discharge from the vulva, which becomes clear, slippery, and stretchy.

kikuyu: Kwaga thuti ya irio; Ng'ombe imwe nīciagaga kūria wega kana kūnyihia mīrire rīrīa īrī na mūrukī.
english: Reduced Appetite: Some cows experience a decrease in appetite during estrus.

kikuyu: Gūitīkīra kūrūgama yahutio mūgongo-inī na īkahorera, kwonania atī nī ihinda riayo ria kūheo ndume. Murimi ni abatiī kūmenya mūtugo wa ng'ombe irenda ndume.
english: Standing Heat: When pressure is applied to the cow’s back, she stands still, indicating she is in heat and receptive to mating. A farmer should be keen to detect the signs by understanding the behaviours of the cows.

kikuyu: Hihi īngīmenya atīa ndume iria īrī na maūthi mega mangīhotithia gūthondeka rūūru hamwe na gūteithia ng'ombe ciakwa kuongerere iria?
english: How do I select suitable sires or bulls for AI to improve genetics and production traits in my dairy herd?

kikuyu: Rūgano rwa bamīrī ya ndume īyo nī rwabata hīndī ya gūcagūra ndume.
english: Pedigree information is important at breed selection point tells us about the genetic stock from which the animal is produced.

kikuyu: Riboti ya ciana cia ndume nī ya bata mūno tondū nī ītūonagia na gūtwira kīria ndume īyo iraciarithia kana kūhe mori yacio.
english: Data on siblings is more valuable, because this tells us what has been potentially passed down to the individual.

kikuyu: Ūū ni kūhītūkia maūndū mega kūrī njiarwa.
english: This is known as heritability.

kikuyu: Ndumīrīri irīa njega ya ndume yonekaga mori-inī, tondū nīītwīraga kīria yaheire mwarī
english: The best information is gained when the animal has offspring, because this tells us what the animal is capable of passing on to future generation

kikuyu: Ng'ombe iria irutaga iria rīingi, ibataraga irio irī na ūtonga mūnene wa nutrients nīgwo ithondeka iria.
english: The high producing dairy cow requires a diet that supplies the nutrient needs for high milk production.

kikuyu: Ūtonga ūyū ūrīa nī hamwe na carbohydrates, amino acids, fatty acids, cumbī, vitamins na maaī ūhotithagia ng'ombe guthondeka iria na indo ria ikoragwo iria-inī.
english: Carbohydrates, amino acids, fatty acids, minerals, vitamins, and water are all nutrients required by the lactating dairy cow to meet the demand by the mammary gland to produce milk and milk components.

kikuyu: Hihi nī mathīna marīkū kaingī mahotomagia ūciari harī ng'ombe cia iria na mangīgirīrīrio atia?
english: What are the most common reproductive disorders in dairy cows, and how do I prevent and manage them?

kikuyu: Mathīna maya mangīrigīrīrio na njīra ya ūtungata mwega wa ng'ombe na kūhūthīra dawa.
english: These disorders may be controlled effectively with improved management practices and appropriate administration of pharmacological and biological agents.

kikuyu: O na kūrī ūguo, ūmenyo wa ica ikuhī oronania atī ihinda rīu rīagīrīirūo kūnyiha kuuma mathaa 16 nginya 6 mbere ya ihinda rīa kuura, na ūndū ūcio ūgatūma ihinda rīrī rīkuhīrīrie ithaa rīrīa mūrūkī ūthiragīra.
english: However, recent findings suggest this interval should be reduced to 16 to 6 h before ovulation, bringing it closer to the end of estrus

kikuyu: Kūmenya tene ng'ombe iria itarī na mahu na mori thutha wa gūcihe mūbira no kūrehe ūhotani wa gūciarithia kaingī na njīra ya kūnyihia ihinda riria ng'ombe yoyaga kuuma yaheo mūbira nginya ūria ūngī
english: Early identification of non-pregnant dairy cows and heifers post breeding can improve reproductive efficiency and pregnancy rate by decreasing the interval between AI services and increasing AI service rate.

kikuyu: O ūrīa ng'ombe īrakuhīrīria gūciara, hebata gūcīongerera mūigana wa protein na gīcunjīgia 20% na mūigana wa 16% wa irio iria ithīīkaga naihenya nīguo gūcīhotithia gūtwarana na gūkūra kwa naihenya kwa njaū iria irī ndaa.
english: As mature cows move from mid to late gestation, they need a 20 percent increase in crude protein intake and 16 percent increase in total digestible nutrient intake to keep up with increasing fetal growth.

kikuyu: Bata ūyū wa kuongerera irio makīria wīyonanagia wega thutha wa ng'ombe gūciara nīguo īhote kūruta iria ria njaū.
english: This need for additional nutrients is magnified once a cow calves and must produce milk for a calf

kikuyu: Ingīhota atīa gūciarithia ng'ombe wega nīguo nyihie moritū marīa mangīoneka nayo njaū īciarwo īna ūgima mwega wa mwīrī?
english: How do I manage calving and parturition to minimize complications and ensure calf health?

kikuyu: Kūrora wega ndariri cia gūciara nī gwabata nīūndū nīgūteithagia kūmenya kama ng'ombe nīgūbatara gūteithio gūthukuuma njaū.
english: Close observation of labor is necessary to determine when or whether a delivery should be assisted.

kikuyu: Gūtangīka rīrīa ng'ombe īraciara kūgayanagio na marūngo matatū; Kīrūngo kia mbere kiambagīrīria nyūngū ya mwana yambīrīria kūhinyīrīrīka, njīra ya ūciri īkaarama na mūthia mathambia njaū magaitīka. Ūūndū ūyū no woye kuuma ithaa rimwe nginya mīrongo irī na īna, no kaingī rioyaga ithaa rīmwe nginya mathaa mana.
english: Labor is divided into three stages:Stage 1 begins with uterine contractions and dilation of the cervix and ends with passage of the amnion and part of the fetus into the vagina. This stage may last 1–24 hours; 1–4 hours is normal.

kikuyu: Ng'ombe ngūrū noyage gūkīria mathaa matatū angīkorwo njaū nīīkaire wega, no angīkorwo hatirī ūgarūrūkū ūkuoneka thutha wa ithaa rīmwe, nīwega kūmīteithia. Ūteithio ūtarī wabata no ūhīngīce ūciari.
english: A mature cow should calve in < 3 hours if presentation of the calf is normal; if no progress is evident within 1 hour, assistance may be required.Inappropriate intervention or social-group stresses may disrupt labor.

kikuyu: Mūtaratara mwega wa gūciarithia ng'ombe nī ūrīa ūtarutaga ng'ombe īyo gīkundi-inī kīrīa īmenyerete yakūhīrīria gūciara nīūndū nīītangīkaga makīria, īkaremwo kūrīa, ona no īhūne.
english: Appropriately timed calving strategies are based on the need to minimize social-group changes at the point of calving, because these social changes are associated with challenges to the intake of dry-matter feed, as well as disrupted labor and increased risk of stillbirth.

kikuyu: Irio cia mbere cia njaū nī gīthana na yagīrīire kūnyua kuuma rita ithatū mathaa-inī merī kuuma yaciarwo.
english: The first feed of colostrum should be at least three litres. This should be fed within the first two hours of birth.

kikuyu: Gīthana kīheyaga njaū hinya wa kūīgitīra kuunama na mīrimū mbere ya njamuthi ciingīrīte mara-inī na nda.
english: This provides the calf with immunity to disease before pathogenic organisms can become established in the calf's gut.

kikuyu: Ingīka atīa kūrigīrīria thīna wa ng'ombe kūgiīka na kūremwo nī gūciara?
english: How do I prevent and manage dystocia (difficult calving) in dairy cows?

kikuyu: Njīra īmwe ya kūrigīrīria mathīna ma guciara nī kweheria mori iria irī na cīiga nini rūūru-inī, na kerī, kūhūthīra ndume iria iciaraga njaū itarī na ūritū mūnene.
english: A combination of culling heifers with small pelvic areas and using bulls that sire calves with small birth weights may decrease dystocia substantially.

kikuyu: Ningīgūkomia ng'ombe rīrīa īraciara na mwena wa ūrio nīgūteithagia njau īingīre mahīndī-ini īrūngīrīirie gūkanyihia thīna wa kūremwo nīgūciara.
english: Positioning of the cow on her right side allows the frontward calf to enter the pelvis of the cow relatively straight.

kikuyu: Ūritū wa kūgucīa njaū ndwagīrīirūo gūkorūo ūrī mūnene gūkīra hinya wa mūndū ūmwe anyitīte kūgūrū na īgūcio ītegūkūjwo
english: Type and amount of traction should be no more than the force of one person per leg and the direction of pull should be straight out

kikuyu: Ningī ng'ombe no igīe na moritū ma kūgwatia mahinda moku.
english: Cows may experience negative impacts on fertility in the subsequent lactation.

kikuyu: Aranīria na ndagītarī wa mahiū rīrīa ng'ombe yaku īkwaga kūgūithia thigira nīūndū ng'ombe noīkue thutha wa kahinda kanini.
english: Always seek your veterinarian's advice on treating cows with retained placenta as the condition can deteriorate into a life-threatening one in a very short period of time.

kikuyu: Kaingī hatirī bata wa kuruta thigira na moko hatarī ūtari wa ndagītarī wa mahiū thutha wa gūthūrima ng'ombe.
english: It is usually not necessary to manually remove the placenta; however, your veterinarian can advise you better after examining the animal.

kikuyu: Nī kūrī maūndū maigana ūna ma bata marīa mangītūma ūciari wa mori ndūkahotome, marīa nī hamwe na;
english: There are a number of key areas for improving fertility management these include:

kikuyu: I) Gūthuura ng'ombe njega cia gūciarithania
english: i) genetic selection (including improved phenotypes for use in breeding programmes),

kikuyu: iii) Kūgitīra mori kuumana na mīrimū ya kūgwatania.
english: iii) control of infectious disease

kikuyu: Nī mītaratara īrīku ya njajo yagīrīire kūrūmīrīrwo nīguo īteithie kūgitīra ng'ombe kūrwara mīrimū īrīa īhotomagia ūciari?
english: What are the recommended vaccination protocols to prevent reproductive diseases in dairy cattle?

kikuyu: Nīguo kūgitīra ng'ombe irī mahu, nīwega irī mori gūcihe njajo igīrī cia BOVI SHIELD GOLD FP kana PREGGUARD GOLD FP. Njajo ya kerī īrūmīrīre thikū 30 mbere ya mori kūheo mūbira.
english: To help ensure safety in pregnant cattle, heifers must receive at least 2 doses of any BOVI-SHIELD GOLD FPor PREGGUARD GOLD FP vaccine with the second dose administered approximately 30 days prebreeding.

kikuyu: Nī mītaratara īrīkū mīagīrīru ya kūruta mūrīmi kūiga rekodi wega?
english: What are the best strategies for training farm personnel on proper record-keeping practices?

kikuyu: Rekodi ciagiriirwo kūigwo kwa njīra hūthū ta njīra ya karamu na karatathi kana kabuku, ledger cia ūrīmi kana recodi cia wonjoria.
english: Recording keeping should be kept simple. This can include Paper – ” method, pen and paper or notebook, ledger book specific to production and/or financial records.

kikuyu: Njīra ici nīihūthīraga mahinda maingī na rīngī ikagīa mahītia no nī njīra njagīrīru kūrī arīmi arīa matarī na ūmenyo wa kūhūthīra computer na arīmi arīa anini.
english: This method requires more time with potential errors, but is favorable to farmers not familiar with computers and small holder farmers.

kikuyu: Njīra iyo ingī nī kūhūthīra mītambo ya kompiuta ona gūtuīka mūrīmi no nginya akorwo na ūmenyo wa kūhūthīra kompiuta, ona mathaa ma gūthondeka fomu na kūihūria rīthiti atekūhītia.
english: Electronic – spreadsheet (Microsoft Excel Google Sheets, etc.), however, the farmer must have a basic knowledge of computers, time to learn the software, design the form, and enter the receipts correctly.

kikuyu: Nī rīera rīrīkū na tīīri ūrīkū wagīrīire wa kūhanda mīembe?
english: What are the climate and soil conditions for growing mangoes in Kenya?

kikuyu: Urīmi mwega wa maembe ūringanaga na gūthūura mūthemba ūrīa waagīrīire itūra rīanyu, tīīri wa mūgūnda waku na rīera.
english: Mango farming success will depend on you growing a type that is best fit for your farm’s altitude, soil and climate.

kikuyu: Tūkīrora matūra ma kūrīma ma būrūri wa Kenya, mīthemba ya maembe nī īrī:
english: Using Kenya’s agro-ecological zoning, there are two major mango categories;

kikuyu: Mīthemba īrīa īhandagwo gīcūa-inī kan kūndū kūrīa kwaraganu, mita kuuma 0nginya 800 igūrū wa iria.
english: coastal/lowland varieties, these are fit for growing in areas of 0-800 MASL.

kikuyu: Kwa mūhiano Ngowe.
english: Examples are the Ngowe

kikuyu: Nī ūkuona mīthemba īno kwa wūingī matūra-inī ma gīcūa-inī ta Mombasa, Kilifi, Tana-River na Lamu.
english: You will find their huge populations in Mombasa, Kilifi, Tana-River and Lamu areas.

kikuyu: Mīthemba ya matūra matarī irīma nene:
english: mid altitude varieties.

kikuyu: Mīthemba īno yagīraga matūra-inī marīa marī mita 800 nginya 1600 igūrū wa iria.
english: These do well in areas of 800-1600 metres above sea level.

kikuyu: Mahandagwo mūno Embu, Merū, Mūrang’a, Marakwet, Kitui, Machakos na Makueni.
english: They are common in Embu, Meru, Muranga, Marakwet, Kitui, Machakos and Makueni.

kikuyu: Nī mīthemba īrīkū ya maembe yagīrīire kūndū kūrīa kwaraganū?
english: Which varieties of mango are for low and altitudes?

kikuyu: Mīthemba ya kūndū kūrīa kwaraganu (0 – 700m.a.s.l.) nī Dodo, Ngowe, Boribo, na Apple.
english: Varieties for lowland (0-700m a.s.l) are Dodo, Ngowe, Boribo and Apple.

kikuyu: Mīthemba ya kūndū gūtarī īrīma na heho nyingī(Medium Altitude Areas) (1500 m.a.s.l) nī Tommy Atkins, Kent, Haden van Dyke, Sensation na Alphonso.
english: Varieties for medium altitude areas (1500m a.s.l) are Tommy Atkins, Kent, Haden, van Dyke Sensation and Alphonso

kikuyu: Nī maūndū marīkū mabatarainie ūrīmi-inī wa maembe?
english: What are the ecological requirements for growing mangoes in Kenya?

kikuyu: Ona kūrīo ūguo, nī kūrī mīthemba īkaga wega matūūra-inī marī igūrū wa mita 1800 igūrū rīa iria.
english: However, other cultivars are reported to yield well at an altitude of up to 1800 mm.

kikuyu: Maembe moīkaine kūheana magetha mega kūndū kūrīa kūrī na ūrugarī.
english: Mango is known to yield well in a warm tropical monsoon climate.

kikuyu: Mendaga ihinda rīa mīeri ītatū ya riūa, gūgīcoka kuura.
english: It needs a prolonged dry period of about three months, followed by rain.

kikuyu: 1.Ūrugarī ūceragīra 15⁰ C nginya 30⁰C.
english: Temperature range – 15º C to 30º C

kikuyu: 2.Mīembe yendaga mbura mūigana wa milimita 500 nginya 1500 o mwaka.
english: 2. Rainfall - Annual 500mm-1500mm

kikuyu: 3. tīīri - Mūriku (mita ithatū), mūnoru na ūrūrū ūtarakīra gīthimo gīa pH 5.5 nginya 7.5
english: 3. Soils - Deep (3m) fertile, well drained and optimum pH 5.5-7.5

kikuyu: Hihi nī maūndū marīkū magīrīire ūkūria-inī wa maembe?
english: What are the best growing conditions for mango?

kikuyu: Mīembe yendaga ūrugarī ūkīrīte 21⁰ C(70⁰ F) na ūtanyihīire 4⁰ C (40⁰F).
english: Mango trees need a warm environment with a temperature ideally above 21°C (70°F) and a minimum temperature of 4°C (40°F).

kikuyu: Maembe mendaga ihinda rīa mathaa manana o mūthenya ma riūa nīguo mahote kūruta kīro na matunda.
english: Mango trees ideally need 8 hours of sunlight per day to produce flowers and fruit.

kikuyu: Mīembe īkūrīirio nyūngū-inī thīinī wa nyūmba nī yendaga kuumio nja yote riūa.
english: Place pot-grown mango trees outside in summer if possible, to give them sufficient sunlight

kikuyu: Nī bataraitha īrīkū īteithagia mūembe kūruta kīro, gwīkira matunda na kūmatunguhia?
english: Which fertilizer are used to induce flowering and promote good fruit set, size and continued growth at flowering and fruiting stage?

kikuyu: Nī ihinda rīrīkū rīega rīa gwikīra bataraitha mīembe-inī?
english: Best time to apply fertilizers in mango?

kikuyu: Īkīra bataraitha mīeri ītatū nginya ītandatū thutha wa kūhanda mītī ya matunda ta mīembe, mababaī na macungwa.
english: After about 3-6 months, start application of nitrogenous fertilizers (in case of fruit trees e.g. mango, pawpaw, oranges).

kikuyu: īkīra bataraitha ya nitrogen kwa ithimi nini ūtigithukanītie nīguo ndīkore nathī kana ona na maaī.
english: Apply nitrogenous fertilizers in varied intervals to avoid leaching out (downward movement of useful mineral or nutrients in water).

kikuyu: Ona ningī mītī no īkīro thumu mūhīu wega, mūhu na kwarīra mūceng'i handū ha bataraitha.
english: Alternatively, properly prepared farm yard manure or compost, kitchen ash (left from cooking) and mulching can be used in place of fertilizers.

kikuyu: Nīwega kūhe mūtī wothe ūrī na ūraihu wa makīria ma mita īmwe bataraitha ya kūrūmīrīria mūthemba wa CAN mūigana wa gramu magana merī ma mīrongo ītano.
english: Trees should be top-dressed with 250g of CAN per tree at the beginning of each rainy season after the trees attain a height of 1 m.

kikuyu: Tīīri wa mīembe ūtukanagio atīa?
english: What is the soil mixture for mangoes?

kikuyu: 25% mūthanga: wa kūrigīrīria kwaraha kwa maaī ma mbura
english: 25% sand: For that just-right drainage

kikuyu: Nī bataraitha īrīkū ya NPK yagīrīire mīembe?
english: What is the best NPK fertilizer for mango trees?

kikuyu: Mīembe īkenagio mūno nī potassium.
english: Mango trees have a thing for potassium.

kikuyu: Mūtukanio wa bataraitha wa 8-3-9 ūkoragwo ūrī mwega tondu ndūkīragia Nitrogen na nīūheaga mūembe potassium ya kūigana.
english: An 8-3-9 fertilizer hits the sweet spot, offering a potassium-rich mix that doesn't go overboard on the nitrogen.

kikuyu: Nīwega kūmenya atī wūingī wa mahuti tikuo kūingīhia matunda.
english: Remember, more leaves don't mean more fruit

kikuyu: Hihi nīrī batiī kūhanda mbeū ya mūembe tīīri-inī?
english: When should I put my mango seed in soil?

kikuyu: Hihi thumu wa ng’ombe nī mwega kūrī mīembe?
english: Is cow manure good for mango trees?

kikuyu: Rūrūa rūngītukanio na maaī nīrūhūthīkaga ta bataraitha na rūtukanagio na tīīri gītīna-inī kia mūembe.
english: Cow dung mixed with water should be used as fertilizer and mixed into soil near the base of a newly planted mango tree.

kikuyu: Hihi thumu wa ngūkū nī mwega kūrī mīembe?
english: Is chicken manure good for mango trees?

kikuyu: Ndūgekīre thumu wa ngūkū kana bataraitha na ihenya thutha wa kūhanda mīembe yaku.
english: Do NOT use chicken manure or fertilise too soon after planting.

kikuyu: Itagīrīria mīembe yaku maaī o thutha wa thikū igīrī.
english: DO water regularly (every second day).

kikuyu: Mīembe īcehagwo atīa?
english: What is the best way to prune mangoes?

kikuyu: Mūembe wagīrīirwo gūcehwo ūrīmū nini.
english: The best way to keep a mango tree small is to prune it when it is young.

kikuyu: Kaingī nī wega gūceeha honge ciothe iria ikīrītie ūraihu wa mita īmwe ūcitige irī cia mita īmwe.
english: As a general rule, prune any branch that is more than a meter in length to about a meter.

kikuyu: Rūmīrīra gūceha honge ciakinyia ūraihu wa inji inyanya.
english: Then make additional cuts every time the branches grow to eight inches.

kikuyu: O maembe magethwo, mītī īgacehwo īkīharīrīrio kīmera kīria kīrumīrīire na kūmīiga īrī na hinya.
english: After every harvest you should make another pruning to prepare the tree for the next season and to keep it healthy.

kikuyu: Ceeha ūkīhūthīra magathī ūkīrutaga honge īria nguū na iria ndwaru.
english: This should be done with lopping shears, you can also prune dead branches and those with diseases.

kikuyu: Tigagīrīra tīīri nī mūigū no ti mūcagacu.
english: Make sure the soil is moist but not drenched.

kikuyu: Rekaga tīīri ūūme hakuhībiū ūtanahe maaīringī.
english: Let the soil dry out almost completely between watering.

kikuyu: Heyaga mīembe maaī maita maingī, no ndūgakīragie.
english: Water your mango tree regularly, but do not overwater it.

kikuyu: Mīrimū na tūtambi: Mīrimū na tūtambi no īgūthūkīrie mūgūnda wothe kana ītūme mīembe īciare matunda matarī mega na gūcūngīrīria hathara.
english: Pest and diseases – Mango pests and diseases can wipe out your mango orchard, or make your mango harvest be of inferior quality, leading to losses.

kikuyu: Mūtungatīre mūru wa mīembe: Arīmī aingī nī magaga gūtungata mīembe igīkūra na kwīrūmbūiya tu hīndī ya magetha.
english: Poor Management – Most mango farmers ignore their mango trees, only paying attention during harvest time.

kikuyu: Mītī ītigagwo īkūre o urīa īkwenda, itagūcehwo kana kūgitīrwo kuumana na mīrimū, tūtambi, na maūndū mangī.
english: The trees are left to scatter on the farm and grow as they wish, without any activities like pruning, disease control, pest control, etc.

kikuyu: Mīembe īngītungatwo wega no īgīe na magetha mega na kūingīhia umithio.
english: Proper management activities of the mango orchard can lead to good quality harvests, hence more income.

kikuyu: Ūndū ūyū ūtigaga arīmi moko-inī na brokers iria ithukagia thogora wa maembe.
english: This leaves them at the mercy of brokers, who dictate meager prices.

kikuyu: Mūrīmi angībanga wega, amenye akagetha maembe maigana atīa, na amenye akendia kū, ūrīmi wa maembe no ūkorwo ūrī biashara ya kwīrirīrio.
english: If you plan early, project your harvest, and identify a target market, then mango farming will be a lucrative venture.

kikuyu: Mbegū ītakinyanīirie ikīro: Arīmi aingī mahandaga mbeū cia kīmerera handū ha īrīa jiarithanie iria iciaraga mbere ya īrīa ītarī jiarithanie.
english: Poor Planting Material – Most mango farmers germinate seeds from the available indigenous seeds, instead of going for the grafted seedlings that start bearing fruit earlier than the ungrafted counterparts.

kikuyu: Mīembe mīciarithanie nī mīhūthū gūtungata na īciaraga mūno.
english: Grafted mangoes are easier to manage and are more productive.

kikuyu: Gūthūka kwa maembe magethwo: Maembe būrūri-inī wa Kenya makorawo na kīmera kīmwe.
english: Post-harvest Losses – Mangoes in Kenya are harvested during one season.

kikuyu: Ūndū ūyū ūtūmaga kūgie na wūingī wamo thoko-inī.
english: This leads to a glut in the market.

kikuyu: Hīndī ya magetha, maembe maingī nī moraga nīundū wa kwaga kūndū kwega gwa kūiga na miumīrīrie mīega.
english: During the mango season, lots of fruit goes to waste because of a lack of proper storage and transport to the market.

kikuyu: Hihi mīembe īitagīrīrio maaī rī?
english: When do you irrigate mango trees?

kikuyu: Mīembe ībataraga maaī manīnī gūkīra mīmera īrīa īngī ya matunda ta marigū.
english: Mango trees need less water than other commercial fruit tree farming like banana farming.

kikuyu: Mīembe yagīrīirwo gūitīīrīrio maaī o thutha wa mīthenya īrī kana ītatū mwaka-īnī wa mbere.
english: Mango farm should be irrigated at an interval of two to three days, in the first year of your mango farming business.

kikuyu: Ona kūrī ūguo, mīembe yambīrīria gūciara yendaga maaī maita meerī.
english: However, at the stage when they start to bear fruit about two irrigations are required.

kikuyu: Mīembe iciarīte ībatiī gūitīīrīrīo maaī o thutha wa thikū ikūmi nginya ikūmi na ithano.
english: You must give water to the fruits bearing plant at an interval of 10 – 15 days.

kikuyu: Mīembe ītigaga gūitīīrīrīo maaī yarīkia kūgimara.
english: Irrigation should be stopped after their full growth.

kikuyu: Mīembe ībatiī kūmenyererwo makīria rīrīa īkūīte kīro.
english: Take proper care during the flowering stage.

kikuyu: Hīndī īno,mīembe ndīkaheo maaī.
english: During this stage, stop giving them water.

kikuyu: īngīaga gūtiga kūheo maaī, mīembe no īciare matunda matarī mega.
english: However, if irrigation does not stop, it may lead to bad quality mango fruit production.

kikuyu: Mūgūnda wa mīembe ūrīmagīrwo atīa?
english: How to control weeds in mangoes?

kikuyu: Nīguo kūnina riia biū mīgūnda-inī ya mīembe, arīmi magīrīirūo kūhūthīra dawa cia ria.
english: In order to manage weeds effectively in mango orchards farmers should practice chemical weed control.

kikuyu: īno nī njīra itarī goro mūnene na īhonokagia mahinda.
english: This method is cost effective and saves time.

kikuyu: Dawa ya ria ndībatīī kūhutīa mathangū ma mītī ya mīembe kana itina cia mītī īrīa mīnini.
english: The spray should not come into contact with leaves or stems of young trees.

kikuyu: Mītī ya mīembe ībatīī gūcehwo kuuma rī?
english: When should pruning of mangoes start?

kikuyu: Guceha kūbatīe kwambīrīria o tene nīgetha mītīīige wega.
english: Pruning should start early for shaping the tree.

kikuyu: Mītī ya ūraihū wa mita īmwe, ītīnio kīongo na magathī ītīgwo īrī na ūraihu wa 0.6m nginya 0.7m.
english: At 1m high, cut the main shoot back to 0.6-0.7 m below the ring buds with secateurs.

kikuyu: Mutī wahethūka ūthuure makunū matatū kana mana na marekwo makure nginya makinyie ūraihu wa mita īmwe, macio namo matinio makuhīhe nginya sentimita 50 nginya 75.
english: After new growth select only 3-4 outward shoots to grow to branches to 1m length, then cut them back to 50-75 cm length again.

kikuyu: Mīembe mīgīma īcehagwo atīa?
english: How should established mango trees be pruned?

kikuyu: Guceha mītī mīgima nī kūruta honge ciothe iria ndwaru na nyūmū nīgetha mīrimū ndīgathereme.
english: Pruning established trees will involve removing all diseased or dead branches to keep infestation from spreading.

kikuyu: Ceha honge ciothe icunjurīte nīguo matunda matikahutie tīīri.
english: Remove hanging branches to keep fruit from dragging on the ground.

kikuyu: Ceha honge īria irūngiī na ūtige iria ngīgamu īria iheaga mūtī mūhianīre mwega na ūraihu wa ūria wagīrīire.
english: Removal of vertical shoots as opposed to horizontal ones for tree shaping and maintaining the right height.

kikuyu: Ceha honge ciothe ngīgamu ūtigie irī na ūraihu wa sentimita 50.
english: Trim horizontal branches to 50cm length.

kikuyu: Hingura mūtī na njīra ya kweheria honge iria ndumanu gatagatī nīgetha rīera rīcere, ūtheri wa riūa ūkinyīre mūtī wothe na kūhūthia mīhūrīre ya dawa.
english: Open the tree center by removing cluttered branch to allow air and sunlight to reach all parts of the trees to stimulate growth and for ease of spray for any infections.

kikuyu: Mītī yagīrīirwo gūcehwo wiki-inī ya kerī nginya ya kana mbere ya īrute mahūa.
english: Pruning should be done 2-4 weeks before flowering begins

kikuyu: Nī ihinda rīrīkū mīembe ibatiī gūcehwo?
english: When is the best time to prune mangoes?

kikuyu: Thutha wa kūgetha maembe (March – April), no ningī mbere ya kīro gūīkīra mweri-inī wa gatano.
english: Should be done after harvesting period is over (March-April) before the main flush in May.

kikuyu: Ceha gatagatīka mūembe ūkīrutaga honge ciothe iria irakūra irorete gitina.
english: - Open the tree centre by removing all the branches growing towards it

kikuyu: Ruta honge ciothe iria ihīngīcanīte na iria ihumbīranīte.
english: - Remove all the branches crisscrossing and those which are shaded

kikuyu: Ruta honge ciothe irorete na thī nīguo atī rūhonge rūrīa rūgūkorwo rūkuhīrīirie tīīri rūraihīrīrie na mita īmwe.
english: - Remove branches growing downwards such that the lowest branch should be at least 1m above the ground

kikuyu: Hihi mīembe īngīkwo atīa nīguo īrute kīro?
english: How to induce flowering in mangoes?

kikuyu: ūndū ūyū no wīkwo na njīra ya:
english: This can be done through:

kikuyu: Njīra cia kīndūire:
english: Cultural Methods

kikuyu: Gūcinīra mahuti rungu rwa mūembe kahora nīguo mūtī ūtogererwo na wītīkīre kūruta mahūa.
english: - Smudging (moist organic material – grass, leaves etc. is slowly burnt under the tree canopies and the resulting smoke induces flowering)

kikuyu: Gūkurura honge cia mūembe ūthiūrūrūkītie.
english: - Ringing the tree branches

kikuyu: Guceha mīri.
english: - Pruning the roots

kikuyu: Kūhaka mīri cumbī.
english: - Applying salts on the roots

kikuyu: Ūhūthīri wa dawa; - Kūhūra mītī wega mūtukanio wa dawa ya Potassium Nitrate (1%) na sticker na ūgītigagīrira nīyahutia irūngo na mathangū.
english: Chemical Methods - Application of Potassium Nitrate (1%) Solution mixed with a sticker agent (adhesive) on the tree totally drenching its terminals and leaves

kikuyu: Angīkorūo ihinda nīrīagīrīire, mahūa makoneka thikū 10 nginya 14 thutha wa kūhūra dawa īno.
english: - If the timing is right, flowering will emerge 10-14 days after application

kikuyu: Gūkorwo mūtī wīharīirie kūruta kīro nīūndū wa bata mūno.
english: - The readiness of the tree to flower is an important factor for a successful operation.

kikuyu: Njīra īno yonanagia moimīrīra mega mītī-inī īna mathangū matarī maruru kana ona maragaruruka rangi magatwīka ma gītīri na kūnīkanga na inegene mahehenjwo na gūoko.
english: Best results are achieved on trees with leaves that are dull green or greenish-brown and brittle when crushed by hand.

kikuyu: Ningī nī mūtī ūhana gūtindima kana ūtaraciara-Auster kana Culter (Paclobutrazol)
english: The tree should have an appearance of suspended growth or be dormant - Auster or Culter (Paclobutrazol)

kikuyu: īno nī dawa njerū būrūri-inī wa Kenya. Na nīīteithagia gūtereba maciaro na ona gūtūma maingīhe.
english: - New product in Kenya. Also regulate production and one gets much higher yields

kikuyu: Ūrūrū wa tīīrī wa kuuma pH ya 5.5 – 7.5 nīguo wagīrīire. tīīri ūraikūrūkia maaī wega, mūthemba wa loam kana clay nīguo mwega.
english: A pH of 5.5 – 7.5 is preferred. Deep well drained, loam or clay is go

kikuyu: Mīembe iciaraga thutha wa miaka īna ngīnya mūgwanja, no īrīa mīciarithanie (īngītīkīrio) no īciare kuuma mwaka-inī wa kerī.
english: Mango seedlings start to bear fruit within 4-7 years, while grafted trees (if allowed) may bear a few fruits in their second year in the field

kikuyu: Hihi kūhanda indo ingī mīembe-inī nīkūgiragia mūgūnda ūgīe ria?
english: Does intercropping mangoes with other crops reduce weeding?

kikuyu: Kūhandīrīra indo ingī mīaka-inī ya mbere ītatū nīkūnyihagia ngarama ya kūrīmīra.
english: An intercrop in the first three years will reduce the cost of wedding.

kikuyu: Thutha wa mwaka wa kana, kīīruru kia mīembe nīkīgiragia ria kūmera.
english: After the 4th year, the canopy will have reduced the weed incidences

kikuyu: Mūembe ūtaiganītie Potassium ūhanaga atīa?
english: How do mangoes with potassium deficiency look like?

kikuyu: Ūgīaga na mathangū marī na ironda īria ciambagīrīria mīthia-inī.
english: -It is characterized by necrosis of leaf margin which starts from the tip downwards.

kikuyu: Matunda matikoragwo mega ona hanini.
english: -Fruit quality is highly reduced.

kikuyu: Mīrimū na tūtambi ikaugūmīra.
english: -Disease and pest attack as secondary infections

kikuyu: Hihi ūnyihu wa potassium ūrūagwo naguo atīa?
english: How do you control potassium deficiency in mangoes

kikuyu: Rūa naguo na njīra ya gwīkīra bataraitha mīthemba ya muriate ya potash,urea na super phospate.
english: Manage by applying muriate of potash, urea and super phosphate fertilizer

kikuyu: Ndariri cia ūnyihu wa Boron nī irīkū?
english: Boron deficiency symptoms?

kikuyu: Mūembe wūitaga kīro na matunda magakaragacuka.
english: -It is characterized by flower abortion, and also cracking of fruits.

kikuyu: Maroro ma rangi wa tīīri marīa marī igūru wa iembe no maingīre nginya thīinī.
english: -Brown areas can also be seen in yellow fruit pulp

kikuyu: Kīhonia kīa ūnyihu wa boron nī kīrīkū?
english: How to control boron deficiency

kikuyu: He mītī yothe īna ūkūrū wa mīaka ikūmi nginya ikūmi na ītano mūigana wa gramu 250 ya boron o mūtī.
english: Apply 250gm boron per tree (10-15-year-old).

kikuyu: Ndariri cia wagi wa coppers mīembe-inī nīi rīkū na ingīrūo nacio atīa?
english: Copper deficiency symptoms in mangoes and how to manage?

kikuyu: Ndariri ici cionekaga kaingī mīembe-inī mīnini irīa īhetwo bataraitha ya nitrogen īgakīra, mūrūri ndūrī hinya, kūgūithia mathangū, kūūma kwa mīthia ya honge, kūinama kwa honge. Hūūra Copper kana Copper Oxychloride (0.3%) o thutha wa mweri ūmwe.
english: Common in young tree due to heavy nitrogenous fertilizer, the terminal shoot is weak, defoliation and die back of branches, drooping shaped branches. spray copper or copper oxychloride (0.3%) at monthly interval

kikuyu: Ingīka atīa nīguo mūembe wakwa ūkūre na ihenya makīria?
english: How can I make my mango tree grow faster?

kikuyu: Handa mūembe handū harakinyīrwo nī riūa na tīīri-inī ūraikūrūkia maaī wega.
english: Plant the tree in a spot with full sunlight and well-draining soil.

kikuyu: Hūthīra bataraitha thondeke wega īrī na nitrogen nyingī yagūteithia mūtī gūkūra naihenya.
english: Fertilization: Use a balanced fertilizer with higher nitrogen content to encourage fast growth during the growing season.

kikuyu: Mīhe maaī kaingī, makīria mīaka-inī ya kīambīrīria.
english: Watering: Water regularly, especially during the first few years

kikuyu: Nī mīmera īrīkū īngīhandwo mīembe-inī?
english: What are the best intercrops for mangoes?

kikuyu: Nī mīmera mīingī ta mīnathi, areca, ndimū, mbera, mababaī, mūgumo, marigū, biribiri, jack, biribiri no īhandanīrio.
english: Many plants such as coconut, areca, lemon, guava, papaya, fig, banana, jack, pepper, can be grown as intercrops.

kikuyu: Mīembe yakwa īraga gūkūra nīkī?
english: Why is my mango not growing?

kikuyu: Nīkūrī itūmi nyingī īngīgiria mīembe īkūre wega ta kwaga irio, maaī na riūa rīa kūigana.
english: There could be several factors that are causing this, such as a lack of nutrients, water, or sunlight.

kikuyu: Maūndū maya no mateithie gūcokereria gūkūra kwa mūembe:
english: Here are some steps you can take to help restore its growth:

kikuyu: Rora tīīri: Tigīrīra mūembe nī wahandwo tīīri-inī mūnoru na ūtaraiga maaī.
english: Check the soil: Ensure that your mango plant is planted in nutrient-rich soil that drains well

kikuyu: Njīra īyo īkoragwo na makinya maya:
english: The method comprises the following specific steps:

kikuyu: Gūciarithania ngi mweri ūmwe mbere ya mīembe kūruta mahūa;
english: breeding flies one month before the flowing phase of the mango;

kikuyu: Nyama kana thamaki īrabutha īngīteo kūu mūgūnda-inī nīīgūtūma ngi iciaranīre kuo,iria iteithagia gūciarithania kwa mītī rīrīa īracanūka biū.
english: inducing flies with discarded livestock entrails or dead fish or rotten meat to pollinate the mango in the full-bloom phase; .

kikuyu: Nīkīī gītūmaga maembe matūke marī mītī-inī?
english: Why do mangoes split on tree?

kikuyu: Rīera rītagīrīire, ta ūrugarī mūingī, mbura na ūhehu mūnene, no itūme maembe maatūke.
english: The unfavorable weather conditions (high temperature, heavy rainfall and humidity) may be the main reasons for fruit splitting in mango.

kikuyu: Gītūmi kīrīa kīnene gītūmaga mīembe īrute kīro noo yage gūciara nī mūrimū mūrū wa anthracnose ūrīa ūhutagia handū hothe ha mītī īyo, no mūno ūthūkagia mahūa.
english: The main reason why the mango trees flower but not setting fruit is anthracnose disease which attack all part of the trees but most damage occurs to the flower panicles

kikuyu: Bataraitha īngīheo mītī ihinda rīrīa rītagīrīire nī ītūmaga matunda marīa manini magwe.
english: Wrong time of fertilisation can cause the young fruits to fall off as well

kikuyu: Ūyū nī mūtaratara wa gūciarithia na kūingīhia mīmera kuuma ihumo-inī ta mbeū, irūngo, na icunjī ingī cia mīmera.
english: It is the process by which new plants grow from various sources: seeds, cuttings, and other plant parts.

kikuyu: ūrīmi-inī wa maembe, mīembe īciarithanagio kuuma mbeū-inī, na makīria kuuma mīembe-inī ya mīthemba ya kīndūire.
english: In mango farming, propagation is primarily done by seeds especially for the indigenous varieties.

kikuyu: Mīembe ya mūciarithanio yumaga kūrī kūgwatithania mīrūri na itina cia kīndūire.
english: Exotic varieties are obtained by successfully grafting a scion on the indigenous rootstock.

kikuyu: ūndū ūyū ūgatūma mītī mīingī īkorūo īrī mīkuhī.
english: This leads to development of the various dwarf trees.

kikuyu: Hihi mīūngūrwa ya mīembe mīciarithanie īhandagwo rī?
english: When are grafted seedlings ready for transplanting?

kikuyu: Mīūngūrwa ya mīembe mīciarithanie no ihandwo kuuma mweri wa kana nginya wa gatandatū.
english: - Grafted seedlings are ready for transplanting out to the field after 4 – 6 months

kikuyu: Mūngūrwa ndūbatiī gūthamio ūtwarwo kūhandwo mūgūnda-inī ūtarutīte mathangū.
english: - A mango tree must never be transplanted while it is flushing or when the leaves are still tender

kikuyu: Thamia mīūngūrwa thutha wa kūruta mathangū ma keerī.
english: - Transplant after the second flush has hardened

kikuyu: Handa mīūngūrwa mbura yaringa, kana wambe wūite maaī irima-inī nīguo mīri īkore tīīri mūigū.
english: - Transplant at the beginning of rains or water the holes before planting to ensure contact of the roots with moist soil

kikuyu: Handa mīūngūrwa irima-inī, ūrīihūrie na tīīri na ūkindīre hanini.
english: - Plant the young tree into the hole and fill the hole and press the soil around the stem firmly

kikuyu: Kwarīra mahuti ma mūcing'i nīkwagīrīire nīguo kūgiria ria kūmera na kūiga maaī tīīri-inī.
english: Mulching around the tree is recommended to smother weeds and to conserve moisture

kikuyu: Mītī īno mīnini ībatiī kūheo bataraitha mūthemba wa CAN mūigana wa gramu magana merī ma mīrongo ītano o mbura īkīringa thutha wa mītī gūkinyia ūraihu wa mita īmwe. īndī tīīri nīwagīrīire gūthimwo.
english: - Trees should be top dressed with 250g of CAN per tree at the beginning of each rainy season after attaining a height of 1 metre. However, soil analysis is recommended.

kikuyu: Mīūngūrwa mīciarithanie yonekaga kuuma kūrī natharī iria hetūkie.
english: Certified mango seedlings are acquired from registered nurseries.

kikuyu: Mūrīmi no aciarithanie mītīyake ya kīndūire na mīthemba īngīirīa yendekithītio.
english: The farmer can top-work the already existing mango trees to introduce recommended varieties.

kikuyu: mūrīmi no ahande mbeū cia kīndūire acooke aciciarithanie na mīrūri kuuma kūrī mīgūnda īrīa mīhītūkie.
english: Farmers can also plant seeds (local varieties) at farm and later graft using scions from registered mother blocks.

kikuyu: Gūciarithania kwa mīembe nīgwīka atīa?
english: What is grafting in mangoes ?

kikuyu: Nī njīra ya bata ya kūingīhia mītī.
english: • Useful in plant propagation

kikuyu: Nīgūtūmaga mītī īkorūo na hinya nīūndū wa kūgarūrīra ūrīa īrutaga wīra.
english: • Improves the genetic and physiological properties of trees

kikuyu: Nī mūtaratara ūhūthīkaga kūgarūra mūembe mūkūrū ūtuīke wa mūthemba ūngī.
english: The technique is used to convert an already established long-lived mango tree into another variety or cultivar.

kikuyu: Mawega ma ūndū ūyū nī hamwe na atī mūtī ūmwe no ūkūrīrio mīthemba ngūrani ya maembe.
english: The benefits include: One tree may produce different varieties of fruit

kikuyu: Mūtī woyaga ihinda inini gūkūra.
english: • Takes a shorter period for the tree to mature

kikuyu: Mūtī nīūkoragwo na hinya nīūndū wa gītina kīrī na mīri mīega.
english: • Helps maintain a healthy plant with a strong root system

kikuyu: Nīkwerūhagia mītī mīkūrū.
english: • Helps rejuvenate old mango trees

kikuyu: Nī indo īrīkū ībatarainie hīndī ya gūciarithania mīembe?
english: What materials are needed for mango grafting?

kikuyu: Kaingī mīūngūrwa ya mīembe īciarithanagio na njīra ya kūmīrenga mītwe.
english: Usually, mango seedlings are grafted using top/ wedge grafting method.

kikuyu: Indo iria ībataranagia nī hamwe na magathī ma gūceha na kahiū.
english: Required tools and materials: Pruning scissors, scalpel or grafting knife.

kikuyu: Tepu ya kūgwatia kana tūratathi twa mūnyore tūta rīna rangi na tūceke.
english: Grafting tape or soft clear polythene bag cut in strips.

kikuyu: Mīembe yagīrīirwo gūciarithanio mweri-inī ūrīkū?
english: Which month is best for mango grafting?

kikuyu: Gūciarithania mūembe na Modified Cleft Grafting mweri 15 wa gatandatū nīwonanirie kūgwatania wega gūkīra Cleft na Veneer gūtakūmakania nī mūthemba ūrīkū wa mūtī.
english: Propagation of mango by modified cleft grafting during 15 June showed higher percentage of survival in compare with cleft and veneer grafting irrespective of varieties.

kikuyu: O na kūrī ūguo, gīcunjī kīa ūgacīru nīkīarī kīnene mūno mweri-inī wa Juni na njīra ya modified cleft grafting no mwerī-inī wa īnana, gūciarithania na veneer gūkīgacīra makīria.
english: The percentage of success was, however, higher in June by modified cleft grafting but in August by veneer grafting

kikuyu: Hihi nī njīra īrīkū njega ya gūciarithania mīembe?
english: Which grafting technique is best for mango?

kikuyu: Nīkūrī njīra nyingī cia gūciarithania mīembe, no njīra īrīa īhūthagīrūo kaingī nī īrīa mūrūri wīkīragwo thīinī wa cleft kana wedge.
english: A wide range of graft types can be used on mangoes, but the two most common are the whip and the cleft or wedge graft.

kikuyu: Kūhūthīra whip gūciarithania mīembe kūhūthagīrwo mūno nī arīa marutaga wīra natharī-inī cia mītī na angī arīa marī na ūmenyeru mūingī, no arīa angī maciarithanagia makīhūthīra njīra ya wedge.
english: The whip graft is used widely by nursery operators and other highly experienced operators, while the wedge graft is used by most other grafters.

kikuyu: Njīra cīerī cia gūciarithania nī hūthū.
english: Both grafts are quite easy to do.

kikuyu: Kīmera kīrīa kīnene kia maembe Kenya kīambagīrīria rī?
english: When is the main production period of mangoes in Kenya?

kikuyu: Gūkoragwo īmera īgīrī:
english: There are two supply seasons.

kikuyu: Kia mbere kīambagīrīria mwerī wa ikūmi na ūmwe nginya wa mweri wa kerī nakīo gīa keerī ngīkambīrīria mweri wa juni nginya wa īnana.
english: The first and main season runs from November to February and the second from June to August.

kikuyu: Matūra marīa marī igūrū ta Murang’a na Mwea (gītaro gia gatagatī gia būrūri wa Kenya) maembe magethagwo wiki inya nginya ithathatū thutha wa matūra ma gīcua-inī kūrīa maembe maingīhaga mweri-inī wa kerī nginya wa ītatū.
english: In areas of higher altitude such as Murang'a and Mwea(Central Province), the harvest season is 4—6 weeks later than at the coast areas, with a peak in February and March.

kikuyu: Kīmera kia maembe kia būrūri wa Kenya kīrīa kīngīikara mīeri ītano nginya ītandandū, nī gīcindanaga na īmera cia mabūrūrī mangī ta Mexico, Brazil, India, Pakistan, Israel, South Africa.
english: The mango picking season in Kenya competes with that of other mango producing countries (Mexico, Brazil, India, Pakistan, Israel, South Africa) and extends over a period of between 5 and 6 months

kikuyu: Nīkīī kīratūma magetha kuuma mīembe-inī yakwa manyihe?
english: Why do I have a lower production of mangoes?

kikuyu: Ona angīkorwo mīembe nīya mūthemba ūmwe ,mūigana wa magetha no ūkorwo na ūtiganu nīūndū mīembe īkūragio matūra-inī marī na rīera na mītungatīre ītiganīte.
english: Even in the case of the same cultivar, yields vary greatly because mango is grown under widely varying agro climatic conditions and cultural practices.

kikuyu: Nīkīī gītūmaga magetha ma maembe makorūo marī na ngūrani o mwaka?
english: Why do mangoes production differ in a year?

kikuyu: Kaingī mīembe īciaraga maita merī o mwaka kana īgaciara ītekūrūmīrīra mūtugo ūyū na nīngī nī harī mīthemba īmwe ya mīembe iciaraga mūno mwaka ūmwe īgacoka īkanyihia maciaro mwaka ūrīa ūmīrīire.
english: Biennial or irregular bearing occurs often with the mango and it is common for some cultivars to bear heavily in one year and sparsely the next.

kikuyu: Ona kūrī ūguo, hactare īmwe no īgethwo tani mīrongo īrī na ītano ona makīria ya maembe mūthemba wa Kent, Sabine, Tommy Atkins na Keītt.
english: However, it is well known that yields of 25 t/ha and more for Kent, Sabine, Tommy Atkins and Keitt are not uncommon.

kikuyu: Mīembe yoyaga ihinda rīigana atīa gūkūra thutha wa kūruta kīro?
english: How long do mangoes take to mature after flowering?

kikuyu: Kūringana na mūthemba na marīa marigicīirie mūgūnda, mīembe no yoe thikū 90 – 160 gūkūra kuuma rīrīa kīro kīaumire.
english: Depending on cultivars and environmental conditions it takes 90 to 160 days after flowering for Kenya mangos to reach maturity.

kikuyu: Maembe marī mūti-inī ūmwe matiīruhanagīra.
english: Not all fruits on one tree will ripen at the same time.

kikuyu: Maembe mabatiī gūtuo kana kūgethwo rī?
english: When is the best time to pick or harvest mango fruits?

kikuyu: Kaingī maembe matuagwo magarūrūka rangi?
english: The fruits are generally picked when they begin to change colour.

kikuyu: Iembe no rīambīrīrie kūgarūrūka rangi handū hanini rangi ūcio ūcoke ūtūngane itunda rīothe.
english: This may occur first in a small area or the change will cover most of the fruit's surface.

kikuyu: īka īmwe ya mīembe igethagwo maembe maigana atīa?
english: What is the yield of mangoes planted in one īka?

kikuyu: īka īmwe ya mīembe īgethagwo maembe gatagatī-inī ga kiro 12,000-18,000 (maembe 500 – 800 o mūembe o mwaka) kuuma kūrī mītī ya ūkūrū wa mīaka ītano.
english: An īka mango trees yield is from 12,000 kgs to 18,000kg (500 to 800 fruits per tree per year) in a year for a 5-year orchard

kikuyu: Hihi desapping kana delatexing nī gwīka atīa?
english: What is desapping or delatexing

kikuyu: Gūtema mīembe hīndīya magetha nīkuuga atīa?
english: What is trimming during harvest of mangoes?

kikuyu: Hīndī ya gūtuo, maembe matigithanagio na mūtī na njīra ya kūrenga kamūtī karīa kacinyitithanītie gagatigwo kari na ūraihu wa sentimita 3-4 iembe-inī karīa gacokaga kūnyihio gagatigwo karī na ūraihu wa sentimita īmwe.
english: At harvesting fruit is clipped from the tree to leave 3 to 4 cm stalk attached to the fruit which is later reduced (trimming) to 1cm during final packing

kikuyu: Maembe makūrū mamenyekaga atīa?
english: How do you identify mature fruits?

kikuyu: 1. Mūhianīre wa iembe– iembe ikūrū rīkoragwo rīrī na ciande njigananu mwena wa mūti-inī na makai maiyūru (Ngowe).
english: 1. Fruit shape- mature fruit have flat shoulders at the stem end and full cheeks (Ngowe).

kikuyu: 2. Mūhianīre wa ikoro – ikoro rīgakorwo na mūtutu mwerū na rangi ūkagarūrūka kuuma grini nduru nginya ngirini hunyūku.
english: 2. Fruit Peel appearance-peel has white powdery substance, peel color change from dark green to pale green

kikuyu: 3. Ngogoyo ya iembe-Ngogoyo īcenjagia kuuma rangi mwerū nginya rangi wa kīrimū.
english: 3. Fruit pulp - pulp color change from white to light creamy yellow.

kikuyu: 4. Ciande njakīku wega– Maembe mūthemba wa Apple magīaga na kariko kanini mwena ūrīa menyiterīire kūrī mūti.
english: 4. Built shoulders- slight depression near the stalk in mature fruit (Apple).

kikuyu: Maembe makūraga na ihinda rīigana atīa?
english: What is the maturity period of mangoes?

kikuyu: Mayoga thikū 95-115 kuuma maruta kīro nginya iembe gūkūra.
english: It takes 95 to 115 day from flowering to fruits maturity

kikuyu: Maembe magethagwo rī?
english: When to harvest mangoes?

kikuyu: Magethagwo kwambīrīria mwaka wa gatatū nginya wa kana kuuma marutwo natharī-inī.
english: Harvesting starts 3-4 years after transplanting.

kikuyu: Mīthemba ngūrani ya maembe īkūraga thutha wa mīeri ītatu nginya ītano kuuma rīrīa mūtī waruta kīro.
english: Fruits are ready 3-5 months from flowering depending on the variety.

kikuyu: Maembe matuagwo magītīgagīrio kamūti karī na ūraihu wa sentimita ithatū nginya inya karīa thutha-inī gakūhīhagio gagatigio karī ka sentimita īmwe.
english: Fruit should be clipped from the tree leaving 3 to 4 cm stalk attached to the fruit which is later reduced to 1 cm

kikuyu: Hihi njīra njega ya kūgetha maembe nī īrīkū?
english: Best way to harvest mangoes fruits?

kikuyu: Hūthīra indo iria ciagīrīire nīguo ūgitīre maembe ūkigetha.
english: Use harvesting tools to help protect fruits at harvesting.

kikuyu: Hūthīra gīkabu kīohereirwo rūbito-inī rūraihu hamwe na kahiū ga gūtua karīa karīnoragwo kaingī nīguo itunda kana mūtī ndūgatihio.
english: Use a basket on a long pole with a cutting tool attached, any blades used for harvesting should be sharpened regularly to minimize damage to the fruit and tree.

kikuyu: Nīūndū wa bata gūthomithia atui ūrīa mabatiī kūhūthīra indo cia gūtua.
english: Proper training before harvesting is key to using harvesting tool correctly.

kikuyu: Maembe mendaga kugethwo rūci-inī tene nīguo maikare marī mahehu na matigate maaī.
english: Harvest fruits early in the day to keep them cool and reduce water loss.

kikuyu: Maembe mairaga nīkī matuo?
english: Why does mango turn black after cutting?

kikuyu: Thīinī wa matunda, nīkūrī tūindo tūītagwo enzymes.
english: Trapped inside the tissue of fruits are molecules known as enzymes.

kikuyu: Enzymes nīcio itumaga matunda meruhe na magaruruke rangi matuīke ma gītīri.
english: These enzymes help fruit ripen and turn brown.

kikuyu: Itunda rīngī temwo kana rīngīambīrīria kūbutha, enzymes irekagīrīrio kuuma thīinī wa itunda igatukana na rīera, igatūma itunda rīgarūrūke rangi naihenya.
english: When fruit is cut or starts to break down, the enzyme is released from the tissue of the fruit and exposed to air which causes the fruit to rapidly change color.

kikuyu: Ūndū ūyū wītagwo enzymatic browning.
english: This is known as enzymatic browning

kikuyu: Gwatūka kwa maembe kūngīrigīrīrio atīa?
english: How do you control fruit cracking in mangoes?

kikuyu: Kūhūra dawa ta naa, potassium na boron mbere ya kūgetha na kūreka tīīri ūige wūigū rīrīa kūrī na riūa ihiū nīkūonekanīte kūrehe ūguni mūnene harī kūgiria maembe gwatūka.
english: Pre-harvest sprays of naa, potassium and boron and maintaining adequate soil moisture during the dry period were found to be beneficial in reducing cracking in fruit crops.

kikuyu: Natharī īrīa njega ya kūhurīra maembe īhana atīa?
english: What is the best suitable nursery for growing mangoes?

kikuyu: Nīkī kīngīrehe kūgaacīra kana kwaga kūgaacīra kwa natharī?
english: This determines the success or failure of a plant nursery:

kikuyu: Natharī ībatiī kūraihanīrīria na mīgūnda īrīa īkūragio maembe ma biacara na ningī īkorwo handū harakīnyīrīka.
english: - A nursery should be isolated as far as possible from existing commercial planting and should be accessible

kikuyu: Gūcera kwa ngari na andū thīinī wa mūgūnda wa natharī gūbatiī kūnyihanyihio.
english: - Movement of vehicles and personnel through the nursery should be limited

kikuyu: Indo ng'eni itigetīkīrio kūingīra mūgūnda-inī wa natharī itathuthurītio wega.
english: - No foreign materials should be allowed into the nursery without proper precautions

kikuyu: Indo ciothe cia kūruta wīra ciagīrīirūo gūtherio wega maita maingī.
english: - Tools and equipment should frequently be sterilized

kikuyu: Maaī makorwo hakuhī na matigakorwo na tūtambi kana njamuthi.
english: - Water should be available and free of harmful pathogens, nematodes and fungi

kikuyu: ūrīa ūngīthuura na gūtungata mīmera īrīa īhūthagīrūo gūciarithania maembe?
english: How to selection and manage mother plants of mangoes

kikuyu: Mbere ya gūthura mbeū, mūndū nīarabatara gūthura na gūīkīra rūūri mītī īrīa mīega īrīhūthagīrwo kūruta mbeū na mīrūri ya gūciarithania.
english: Prior to seed collection, one needs to select and mark good mango mother trees to use as sources of high quality seed and scions.

kikuyu: Ngumo iria nene cia mūtī mwega wa gūciarithania nī hamwe na:
english: The major characteristics of a good mother tree are:

kikuyu: -Gūkūra kwa mūtī
english: - Mature

kikuyu: -Ndūrī na tūtambi na mīrimū
english: - Free of pests and diseases

kikuyu: -Gūkūra na hinya
english: - Vigorous

kikuyu: -Gūciara mūno
english: - High yielding

kikuyu: Njīra ya kūhiūrania na mboca cia iembe nī īrīkū?
english: How to manage and control mango weevil?

kikuyu: Mboca ya nga īrekagīria matumbī maembe-inī marīa macarīkio matuīkaga tūgunyū tūrīa tūingīraga itunda-inī na kūrīrīa nginya rīkagwa rītarī rīrakūra
